'''Percy Romeo Miller''' (born August 19, 1989), also known by his stage name '''Romeo''' (formerly '''Lil' Romeo'''), is an American rapper, singer, actor and television personality.<ref name="Romeo biography1">{{cite web |url=http://music.msn.com/music/artist-biography/lil'-romeo/ |title=Lil' Romeo: Biography |publisher=MSN |access-date=July 16, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130129073001/http://music.msn.com/music/artist-biography/lil'-romeo/ |archive-date=January 29, 2013}}</ref> He gained fame as a rapper in the early 2000s after signing with his father, [[Master P]]'s record label [[No Limit Records]]. His 2001 debut single, "[[My Baby (Lil' Romeo song)|My Baby]]" peaked at number three on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and preceded his debut studio album ''[[Lil' Romeo (album)|Lil' Romeo]]'', which peaked at number six on the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/d12-leapfrogs-keys-returns-to-no-1-79145/|title=D12 Leapfrogs Keys, Returns to No. 1|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=July 12, 2001}}</ref>

In 2002, Miller released his second album ''[[Game Time]]'', which charted at number 33 on the US ''Billboard'' 200. In 2004, Miller released his third album ''[[Romeoland]]'', which charted at number 70, and in 2006, he released the digital album ''Lottery'' under the name '''Romeo'''. That same year, Miller released an accompanying [[God's Gift (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to his film ''[[God's Gift (film)|God's Gift]]''; his first explicit album. To date, it has sold over 300,000 units.

In 2007, Miller was offered and accepted a [[scholarship]] to play [[basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]], at the [[University of Southern California]]. He played basketball for the Trojans under his birth name, and played for the team until 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/blog/the_dagger/post/-Lil-Romeo-s-underwhelming-USC-career-comes-to-a?urn=ncaab,242862|title=Lil' Romeo's underwhelming USC career comes to an end|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|access-date=June 10, 2015}}</ref> Aside from music, Miller has also worked as an actor and was given his own television series on [[Nickelodeon]] titled ''[[Romeo!]]'' in 2002, which ran for three seasons. Miller starred in the feature films ''[[Jumping the Broom (film)|Jumping the Broom]]'' (2011) and [[Tyler Perry]]'s ''[[Madea's Witness Protection]]'' (2012). Miller founded the [[record label]]s Guttar Music, Take a Stand, The Next Generation and [[No Limit Forever Records]] in 2010.

==Early life==
Miller was born in [[New Orleans]], Louisiana.<ref name="Romeo biography1" /> He is a son of rapper and entrepreneur [[Master P]] and former rapper [[Sonya C]].<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://allhiphop.com/2017/07/20/master-p-confronts-romeo-miller-about-letting-the-family-down-in-growing-up-hip-hop-sneak-peek-video/| title= Master P Confronts Romeo Miller About Letting The Family Down In 'Growing Up Hip Hop' Sneak Peek |website= allhiphop.com | date= July 20, 2017 |access-date=2018-01-13}}</ref> He is a nephew of rappers [[C-Murder]] and [[Silkk the Shocker]], cousin of producer, singer, and rapper [[Mo B. Dick]], and a brother of singer and actress [[Cymphonique Miller]]. Romeo was signed to [[No Limit Records|No Limit]]'s subsidiary label Soulja Music Entertainment at the age of five, after he wrote a rap to his father.

==Music career==
===2001: ''Lil' Romeo''===
As Lil' Romeo, his debut album was the self-titled ''[[Lil' Romeo (album)|Lil' Romeo]]''. It contains the hit single "[[My Baby (Lil' Romeo song)|My Baby]]" that charted No. 1 for R&B/Hip-hop Singles. The album peaked at No. 6 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and No. 5 on the [[Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums]]. On July 28, 2001, it was certified Gold by the RIAA for selling 500,000 copies in the United States. Also in 2001, he was featured on his uncle Silkk the Shocker's remix single of "[[Lil' Romeo (album)|That's Kool]]", which was also featured on his own album.<ref name="Romeo biography2"/>

===2002–2003: ''Game Time''===
In 2002, a year later after his debut album, Miller put out his second studio album, ''[[Game Time]]''. It peaked at No. 33 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and No. 10 on the [[Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums]].<ref name="Romeo biography2">{{cite web |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/romeo |title=Percy Romeo Miller, Jr. Biography |website=Billboard.com |access-date=2012-12-15 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927032327/https://www.billboard.com/artist/romeo/ }}{{failed verification|reason=URL looks like it was usurped/page changed since 2012|date=February 2023}}</ref> It spawned the Billboard-charting single "[[2-Way]]" that charted to No. 66 [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]]. It also spawned a second single "True Love" which charted at No. 16 under the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]].<ref name="Romeo biography2"/>

===2004: ''Romeoland''===
In 2004, Miller released his third studio album ''[[Romeoland]]'' via [[No Limit Records|The New No Limit]] and [[Koch Records|Koch]], it would be Miller's last studio album to feature himself billed as Lil' Romeo; it was not as successful in sales.<ref name="Romeo biography1" /><ref name="Romeo biography2"/> ''Romeoland'' charted at No. 70 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and at No. 29 on the [[Top Rap Albums]] chart.

===2005–2007: Collaborations, name change, ''Lottery'' and ''God's Gift'' soundtrack===
In 2005, Miller, along with his father Master P, founded a new record label titled [[Guttar Music Entertainment]]. Also in 2005, Miller, along with his brother Valentino Miller and their three cousins C-Los, [[D The Business|Lil' D]] and Willie J, formed the rap group Rich Boyz. They released their debut album titled ''Young Ballers: The Hood Been Good to Us'' via Guttar Music on November 22, 2005. The group later disbanded.

On April 4, 2006, Miller released his debut digital album ''[[Lottery (album)|Lottery]]'' via Guttar Music Entertainment, UrbanDigital and [[GoDigital Media Group|GoDigital Music Group]], it was Miller's first album released with his official name changed to Romeo. On December 12, 2006, Miller released an album titled ''[[God's Gift (soundtrack)|God's Gift]]'' via Guttar Music, UrbanDigital and GoDigital Music Group, it served as the [[soundtrack]] to the same name independent [[God's Gift (film)|film]] Miller's father Master P had directed and produced, it was also Miller's first album to be classified as [[:wikt:explicit|explicit]].<ref name="Romeo biography2"/> Both albums contained the song "U Can't Shine Like Me", which was a direct response to fellow rapper/actor [[Bow Wow (rapper)|Bow Wow]], who fans believed dissed Miller and his father Master P in his song "[[Fresh Azimiz]]".

In 2007, Miller and his father Master P started a non-explicit record label titled Take A Stand Records. They also formed a new group called Miller Boyz. On September 4, 2007, they would release their debut album titled ''[[Hip Hop History]]'' via Take A Stand Records, UrbanDigital and GoDigital Music Group.

===Since 2008: Mixtapes, EPs and collaborations===
In 2008, Miller stated he was working on his fourth studio album titled ''[[Get Low LP|Gumbo Station]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kidzworld.com/article/10347-romeo-interview |title=Romeo Interview | Chat | Li'l Romeo | USC | Gumbo Station | Master P | Pic |website= Kidzworld.com |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref> On June 17, Miller released the first single from the album "Get Low Wit It", which featured [[Akon]] and his brother Valentino Miller, it failed to gain success on the ''Billboard'' charts.<ref>{{cite web|last=Side |first=My |url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/get-low-wit-it-feat-akon/id280745904?i=280745990 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715074714/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/get-low-wit-it-feat-akon/id280745904?i=280745990 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 15, 2014 |title=Get Low Wit It (feat. Akon) – EP by Romeo – Download Get Low Wit It (feat. Akon) |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=June 17, 2008 |access-date= November 19, 2011}}</ref>

On March 3, 2009, Miller released a [[compilation album]] titled ''[[Get Low (album)|Get Low]]'' that contained singles that were originally supposed to have been on ''Gumbo Station'' and also contained original songs from his previous albums. In late 2009, Miller formed a new [[record label]] titled The Next Generation Entertainment, the label at the time featured his group the College Boyys.<ref name="Romeo leaves USC to focus on music">{{cite web|first=Danielle|last=Canada|url=http://hiphopwired.com/2010/01/08/romeo-leaves-basketball-behind-focuses-on-new-music/ |title=Romeo Leaves Basketball Behind, Focuses On New Music|website= Hiphopwired.com |date=January 8, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref>

During this time, Romeo also confirmed that he was still working on his fourth studio album, but had changed the name of the album to ''The College Boy''. Later, Romeo announced that the title of the album would be ''I Am No Limit''. On January 19, 2010, Miller released a promotional single for the album titled "Tell Me a Million Times" featuring Tempo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/tell-you-a-million-times-feat-tempo-single/353904479 |title=Tell You a Million Times (feat. Tempo) – Single by Romeo – Download Tell You a Million Times (feat. Tempo) |publisher= iTunes Music Store |date=January 19, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref> On January 26, Miller released a second promotional single for the album titled "Ice Cream Man Jr." which was a tribute to his father.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/ice-cream-man-jr-feat-valentino/id353938007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714134245/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/ice-cream-man-jr-feat-valentino/id353938007 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |title=Ice Cream Man Jr. (feat. Valentino and Black Don) – Single by Romeo – Download Ice Cream Man Jr. (feat. Valentino and Black Don) |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=January 26, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref> On February 16, Miller released his debut mixtape ''Patience Is A Virtue'' to promote the album.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://percyromeomiller.blogspot.com/2010/02/go-download-patience-is-virtue.html |title=Romeo: Go Download "Patience Is A Virtue" |website= percyromeomiller.blogspot.com |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date= November 19, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824072142/http://percyromeomiller.blogspot.com/2010/02/go-download-patience-is-virtue.html |archive-date=August 24, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> On March 2, Miller released two [[extended play|EP]]s to promote the album which were the ''Famous Girl'' and ''Monster/Practice'' via his label The Next Generation Entertainment and LPD Music.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://music.apple.com/us/album/monster-feat-tempo-practice/362887340 |title=Monster (feat. Tempo) / Practice – Single by Romeo – Download Monster (feat. Tempo) / Practice |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=March 2, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/famous-girl-feat-sean-kingston/id362885123 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140720013347/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/famous-girl-feat-sean-kingston/id362885123 |url-status= dead |archive-date= July 20, 2014 |title=iTunes Store |publisher=iTunes Music Store |access-date= November 19, 2011}}</ref> Also in 2010, Miller would introduce his new group the College Boyys; on May 25, 2010, they released their debut album titled ''Spring Break'' via his label The Next Generation Entertainment and Hollywood Dream Music, but the group would later disband for unknown reasons.<ref>{{cite magazine| url= https://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003817568#/album/college-boyys/spring-break/1329575/review |title=Lil Wayne Cracks 1 Million With 'Tha Carter III' |magazine=Billboard |access-date=November 19, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110913134450/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003817568 |archive-date=September 13, 2011 }}</ref> Miller also on this day released three promotional singles which were "You" that featured his artist at the time D'Anna and [[Lil Twist]], "She Bad" that featured his cousins/artists [[D The Business|Lil' D]] and [[Black Don]] and "They Dont Know".<ref>{{cite web |url= https://music.apple.com/us/album/you-feat-lil-twist-danna/377043640?i=377043656 |title=You (feat. D'anna and Lil' Twist) (Single) by Romeo – Download You (feat. D'anna and Lil' Twist) (Single) on iTunes |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=May 25, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/she-bad-feat-black-don-lil-d/377043642?i=377043661 |title=She Bad (feat. Black Don and Lil' D) – Single by Romeo – Download She Bad (feat. Black Don and Lil' D) |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=May 25, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/they-dont-know-prod-by-riley/377043709 |title=They Don't Know (Prod. by Riley J) (Single) by Romeo – Download They Don't Know (Prod. by Riley J) (Single) on iTunes |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=May 25, 2010 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref> Miller also performed at the 2010 [[Hip Hop Honors]] along with his brother Valentino Miller, his cousins [[D The Business|Lil' D]] and Black Don, and his uncle Silkk The Shocker, along with [[Trina]], [[Gucci Mane]] and [[Mystikal]] to honor Master P and [[No Limit Records]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vh1.com/video/shows/2010-hip-hop-honors/525475/2010-hip-hop-honors-tribute-performance-master-p.jhtml |title="2010: Hip Hop Honors Tribute Performance: Master P" | Show Clip |work=VH1 |access-date=November 19, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209182452/http://www.vh1.com/video/shows/2010-hip-hop-honors/525475/2010-hip-hop-honors-tribute-performance-master-p.jhtml |archive-date=February 9, 2012 |df=mdy }}</ref> In late 2010, Miller relaunched No Limit Records as [[No Limit Forever]]. Romeo also confirmed that he had changed the name of his album from ''I Am No Limit'' to ''Intelligent Hoodlum''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nolimitforeverrecords.com/?p=27 |title=Romeo: Intelligent Hoodlum |publisher=No Limit Forever Records |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref>

In 2011, Miller toured with his father and Silkk the Shocker. The tour was titled "No Limit Forever International".<ref>[http://www.trutanksoldiers.com/forum/topics/no-limit-forever-international No Limit Forever International Tour – Coming in 2011! Ughhh! Ft Master P, Silkk, Rome & more! – TTS – Master P, No Limit Records, TRU & No Limit Forever Records] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110126085450/http://www.trutanksoldiers.com/forum/topics/no-limit-forever-international |date=January 26, 2011 }}</ref> On January 11, Miller released his EP ''Dont Push Me'' via his label The Next Generation Entertainment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/dont-push-me/413309165 |title=Don't Push Me by Romeo – Download Don't Push Me on iTunes |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=January 11, 2011 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref> On May 3, 2011, Miller released the first official single from ''Intelligent Hoodlum'' called "Famous Girl (Remix)" which was the mastered version of the original, it still featured the original appearances from [[Sean Kingston]] and Miller's cousin Black Don, but it would be later dubbed as a promotional single.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/famous-girl-remix-feat-sean/id434317312 |title=Famous Girl (Remix) [feat. Sean Kingston] – Single by Romeo – Download Famous Girl (Remix) [feat. Sean Kingston |publisher=iTunes Music Store |date=May 3, 2011}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On August 19, 2011, Miller released his ''I Am No Limit'' mixtape, which was originally supposed to be his fourth studio album, but Miller decided it would be best to just release it as a mixtape for his fans.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.ilovepwnage.com/video.php?v=MjM5Mjk |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220319064847/http://www.ilovepwnage.com/video.php?v=MjM5Mjk |url-status= dead |archive-date= March 19, 2022 |title=Video: Romeo – I Am No Limit [Behind The Scenes Footage] |website= Ilovepwnage.com |access-date= November 19, 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.datpiff.com/Romeo-I-Am-No-Limit-mixtape.262809.html |title=Romeo – I Am No Limit Hosted by No Limit // Free Mixtape | website= Datpiff.com |date=August 19, 2011 |access-date=November 19, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hotnewhiphop.com/en/view-album/21222-i-am-no-limit |title=Romeo – I Am No Limit |website= Hotnewhiphop.com |date=August 19, 2011 |access-date=November 19, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20111011173604/http://www.hotnewhiphop.com/en/view-album/21222-I-Am-No-Limit |archive-date=October 11, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

In 2012, Miller formed a new group called Resq3 which consisted of himself, drummer Christian Brock and guitarist/vocalist Myles Eberhardt. They released their first single "The Only One" and were scheduled to be releasing their debut album, touring and filming TV show later that year, but the group would disband for unknown reasons. The group's other releases consisted of songs such as "Right Along" and "No One Else Like You".<ref>{{cite web| url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M0rLW0saOpA | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211118/M0rLW0saOpA| archive-date=2021-11-18 | url-status=live|title= Romeo Miller's RESQ3 Band Interview at Popstar! Magazine '12 in 12' Event| via= YouTube |date= 2011-12-07| access-date= 2012-12-15}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2012/02/romeo-miller-re-teams-with-tom-lynch-for-musical-sitcom-238165/|title=Romeo Miller Re-Teams With Tom Lynch For Musical Sitcom|first=Nellie|last=Andreeva|date=March 1, 2012 |website= [[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=December 30, 2017}}</ref> On April 12, 2012, Miller released his first single from his upcoming fourth album titled "Hug Me Forever", which featured his brother Valentino. On May 19, 2012, Miller released the music video for "Hug Me Forever".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qgKkAynLb78 Romeo "Hug Me Forever"]. YouTube (2012-04-12). Retrieved on 2012-12-15.</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5ywpEALPCU Romeo Miller Feat. Valentino & Kyros – Hug Me Forever]. YouTube. Retrieved on 2012-12-15.</ref> On August 15, 2012, Miller announced that he had been working on a new mixtape titled ''Inception'', it was released on August 19, 2012, under his new stage name Maserati Rome.<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.trutanksoldiers.com/?p=971 |title= Inception (Mixtape) Download Now! | website= TruTankSoldiers.com | publisher= No Limit Forever Records| date= 2012-08-15| access-date= 2012-12-15}}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2013, Miller announced that he was working on a mixtape, ''When in Rome'', slated for release in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hl4uGAa3UGE | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130717065939/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hl4uGAa3UGE&gl=US&hl=en| archive-date=2013-07-17 | url-status=dead|title=Romeo in studio making of the "Irrelevent" [sic] song |via=YouTube |date=2013-07-16 |access-date=2014-02-24}}</ref>
On January 5, 2015, Miller released his first collaboration mixtape titled ''We All We Got'' with his group Money Mafia that includes himself, his father, Ace B, Young Junne, Eastwood, Gangsta, Play Beezy, Calliope Popeye, Flight Boy and No Limit Forever in-house producer Blaq N Mild. The mixtape would also include a surprise feature from [[Lil Wayne]] on the track "Power".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.datpiff.com/Money-Mafia-We-All-We-Got-mixtape.679360.html|title=Money Mafia – Miller played basketball as a [[point guard]] for one year at Windward High School before he transferred and became a three-year starter at [[Beverly Hills High School]]. As a junior, during the 2005–06 high school season, he averaged 13.9 points and 5.6 assists per game.<ref name=USC-Trojans>{{cite web| url= http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/miller_percy00.html |title= Player Bio: Percy Miller| website= USCTrojans.com| access-date= May 21, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100526044344/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/miller_percy00.html |archive-date=May 26, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=Frost>{{cite web| first= Antracia |last= Merrill-Moorings| url= http://www.frostillustrated.com/full.php?sid=1125 |title= Lil Romeo to shoot hoops for USC| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20070624174409/http://www.frostillustrated.com/full.php?sid=1125 |archive-date=June 24, 2007 | website= FrostIllustrated.com | access-date= May 6, 2007}}</ref> As a senior, during the 2006–07 high school season, he averaged 8.6 points and 9.0 assists per game.<ref name=wsj/><ref name=USC-Trojans/>

In the summer of 2006, Miller was invited to the Reebok-sponsored [[ABCD Camp]], a basketball camp in the US. The [[Teaneck, New Jersey]]–based camp, an invitation-only basketball showcase, was previously attended by high-profile [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) players including [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Stephon Marbury]], [[Tracy McGrady]], [[LeBron James]], and [[Carmelo Anthony]]. Surrounded by future NBA players such as [[O. J. Mayo]], [[Derrick Rose]], and [[Kevin Love]], Miller averaged less than 2 points a game and struggled throughout the camp. Sonny Vaccaro, the longtime director of the ABCD Camp, explained that he invited Miller to the 2006 camp, "primarily as a favor to Percy Miller (Romeo's father [[Master P]]), whom he knew from the club basketball circuit." Vaccaro also said, "If you're looking for the profile of an athlete who plays basketball at USC, he's not it."<ref name=wsj>{{cite news|first= Jon |last= Weinbach |date= March 7, 2008| url= https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB120485166974418241 |title= A Hot Prospect?| work= The Wall Street Journal| access-date=July 28, 2008}}</ref>

Despite this, on April 13, 2007, Miller verbally committed to the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) and signed a letter of intent on November 19. According to ''The Wall Street Journal'', the decision to grant Miller a full scholarship at USC was largely driven by his relationship with friend and teammate [[DeMar DeRozan]], an All-American forward who was rated as the number five prospect in the country on Scout.com, and his father's influence. ''The Wall Street Journal'' reported Coach [[Tim Floyd]] as saying, "Last April ... Percy Miller called while driving both players from a tournament in Fayetteville, Ark ... Percy Miller said 'Demar and Romeo are ready to make their decision, and would you like to have them both on scholarship?' ... 'I said absolutely.'"<ref name=wsj/>

Miller and DeRozan began playing for USC in the [[2008–09 USC Trojans men's basketball team|2008–09 season]]. Miller used his given first name, '''Percy''', when playing for the Trojans. He only played for the Trojans for two seasons, and was released after the [[2009–10 USC Trojans men's basketball team|2009–10 season]]. He played a total of 19 minutes in nine games, scoring five points and recording three rebounds and one assist.

She began her career as a child actress with roles in the 2003 films ''[[The Hunted (2003 film)|The Hunted]]'', ''[[Dickie Roberts: Former Child Star]]'' and ''[[The Missing (2003 film)|The Missing]]'', and the 2005 film ''[[The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants (film)|The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants]]''. She was selected at age two in a modeling search.{{cite news| url= https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/2005/06/01/jenna-boyd-sob-sister/e17e52f0-4d11-4b16-b618-c84521afbf6b/| newspaper= [[Washington Post]] | title=Jenna Boyd: Sob Sister| date= June 1, 2005 | access-date= August 8, 2019}}{{cite news| url= https://www.express.co.uk/showbiz/tv-radio/1017575/Atypical-season-2-cast-netflix-who-is-jenna-boyd-paige-hardaway-actress| website= express.co.uk| title= Atypical season 2 cast: Who is Jenna Boyd? Who plays Paige?| first= Samuel| last= Spencer| date= September 14, 2018| access-date= August 8, 2019}} She and her parents and younger brother [[Cayden Boyd|Cayden]] (also an actor) moved to [[Los Angeles]] to pursue her acting career. In September 2019, she moved to Tulsa, Oklahoma as part of the Tulsa Remote program.{{Cite web|url=http://ktul.com/news/local/actress|title=Actress moves to Tulsa as part of Tulsa Remote program|last=staff|first=Tyler Butler, KTUL|date=September 3, 2019|website=KTUL|access-date=September 6, 2019}} She is a graduate of [[Pepperdine University]], where she earned a business degree.{{cite news| url= https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/bailey-sisterhood-traveling-pants-grown-stunning-skincare-guru-154329963.html | website= Yahoo.com| title= Bailey from 'The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants' is all grown up — and a stunning skin care guru| first= Maggie | last= Parker| date= October 18, 2017 | access-date= August 8, 2019}} ==Career== Boyd began her career at age three, appearing in episodes of the children's TV show ''[[Barney & Friends]]''. She simultaneously acted and figure skated. In ''[[Dickie Roberts: Former Child Star]]'' she played the daughter of a family hired by the titular character ([[David Spade]]) to help him recapture his childhood. Boyd's big break came when she was cast in ''[[The Missing (2003 film)|The Missing]]'', alongside [[Cate Blanchett]] and [[Evan Rachel Wood]]. Although the film itself was not particularly well-received, critics praised Boyd's performance. In 2005 Boyd played [[leukemia]]-suffering Bailey Graffman in ''[[The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants (film)|The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants]]''. She appeared in the [[Lifetime Television|Lifetime]] miniseries ''[[The Gathering (miniseries)|The Gathering]]'' as the daughter of a doctor ([[Peter Gallagher]]) searching for his wife;{{Cite web |last=Lowry |first=Brian |date=2007-10-10 |title=The Gathering |url=https://variety.com/2007/scene/markets-festivals/the-gathering-5-1200555427/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Variety |language=en-US}} and in the ''[[Ghost Whisperer]]'' episode "Children of Ghosts", as a troubled teenager living in a [[foster home]]. '''Vivien Cardone''' (born April 14, 1993<ref name=school/>) is an American actress, known for her role as Doctor Brown's daughter Delia on [[The WB]]'s ''[[Everwood]]'' from 2002 to 2006. She has appeared in ''[[One Life to Live]]'' (2011) and ''Theater, Interrupted'' (2020–2021).

==Early life==
Cardone was born in [[Port Jefferson]], New York. She is one of four children. Her older sister Olivia was an actress. She has a brother and another sister. The Cardone children were homeschooled, Vivien entered school in 2005.<ref name="school">{{cite web |url= http://www.viviencardone.com/ |title= Vivien Cardone |publisher=viviencardone.com |access-date=15 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110226104117/http://www.viviencardone.com/ |archive-date=26 February 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Cardone began her professional acting career at the age of three months in national campaign commercials, for such companies as [[Pizza Hut]], [[Sears]], [[Pillsbury Company|Pillsbury]], and [[Sherwin-Williams]].<ref name="school" /> Her first film performance was as Marcee Herman in the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] winning film ''[[A Beautiful Mind]]''. Her biggest role so far has been in ''[[Everwood]]'', in which she played Delia Brown. She played the role for four seasons, until the show was cancelled in May 2006.<ref name="spy">{{cite web|url= https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a840917/everwood-cast-where-are-they-now/ |title= Everwood – where are Andy, Amy, Ephram, Delia and Bright now?|publisher=digitalspy.com|date=18 October 2022}}</ref> She was nominated for a [[Young Artist Award]] for Best Supporting Young Actress in a TV series for all four seasons.
 
In 2008, Cardone starred in the film ''[[All Roads Lead Home]]''.<ref name="spy"/> In it she plays Belle, a 12-year-old girl who has to cope with the loss of her mother from an automobile accident. It stars [[Peter Coyote]], [[Jason London]] and [[Peter Boyle]] in his last film.<ref name="spy"/> She appeared in an episode of ''[[Law & Order: Criminal Intent]]'' in 2010.<ref name="spy"/> In 2011, Cardone starred as Michelle in eight episodes of ''[[One Life to Live]]''.<ref name="spy"/>

'''Jeremy James Kissner''' (March 24, 1985) is an American actor.

Kissner's first film role was in 1998's remake of ''[[Great Expectations (1998 film)|Great Expectations]]'', playing the younger version of [[Ethan Hawke]]'s character Finn.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Great Expectations' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/greatexpectationshowe.htm#:~:text=when%20finn%20(played%20as%20a%20boy%20by%20jeremy%20james%20kissner)%20returns%20with%20the%20goods,%20the%20convict%20orders%20him%20into%20a%20motorboat%20and%20heads%20for%20mexico. |access-date=2023-09-04 |website=www.washingtonpost.com}}</ref>

After an appearance on the television series ''[[Melrose Place]]'', he starred in the lead role of the 1999 remake of ''[[A Dog of Flanders (1999 film)|A Dog of Flanders]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/1999/film/reviews/a-dog-of-flanders-1117752043/|title=A Dog of Flanders|last=Leydon|first=Joe|date=1999-08-24|website=Variety|language=en|access-date=2020-04-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Nichols|first=Peter M.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/09/03/movies/taking-the-children-a-mild-mannered-mountie-turns-whoops-dastardly.html|title=TAKING THE CHILDREN; A Mild-Mannered Mountie Turns (Whoops!) Dastardly|date=1999-09-03|work=The New York Times|access-date=2020-04-12|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/library/film/082799dog-film-review.html|title='A Dog of Flanders': A Boy. A Dog. You Know the Rest|website=archive.nytimes.com|access-date=2020-04-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/movies/reviews/dogofflandershorwitz.htm|title='A Dog of Flanders' (PG)|website=www.washingtonpost.com|access-date=2020-04-12}}</ref>

Kissner subsequently appeared on several television series, including ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]'' <ref>{{Citation |last=Chulack |first=Christopher |title=Man with No Name |date=2005-10-06 |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0568038/ |access-date=2023-09-04 |series=ER |others=Goran Visnjic, Maura Tierney, Mekhi Phifer}}</ref> and ''[[Touched by an Angel]]'',<ref>{{Citation |last=Peerce |first=Larry |title=A Clown's Prayer |date=2000-05-07 |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0731993/ |access-date=2023-09-04 |series=Touched by an Angel |others=Roma Downey, Della Reese, John Dye}}</ref> as well as in several [[independent films]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brotherhood of Blood |url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/813546/brotherhood-of-blood/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150310150805/http://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/title/813546/Brotherhood-of-Blood/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 10, 2015 |access-date=2023-09-04 |website=Turner Classic Movies |language=en}}</ref>

From 2005 to 2007, he appeared in the [[Discovery Kids]] series ''[[Flight 29 Down]]'' as Eric.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://archives.starbulletin.com/2005/06/21/features/index3.html|title=Honolulu Star-Bulletin|website=archives.starbulletin.com|access-date=2020-04-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://the.honoluluadvertiser.com/article/2006/Feb/12/il/FP602120319.html|title='Flight 29 down' takes off |work=Honolulu Advertiser|access-date=2020-04-12}}</ref>

'''Sophie Oda''' (born October 23, 1991) is an American actress and singer. She was nominated in 2007 by the Young Artist Awards as a guest starring young actress.

==Personal life==
Oda, a Japanese American,<ref name="about">[http://www.sophieoda.com/About_Sophie.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100824080918/http://www.sophieoda.com/About_Sophie.html|date=August 24, 2010}}</ref> performed in Asian Americans on Broadway,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Asian_Americans_on_Broadway_Opening_Doors_20060923 |title=Asian Americans on Broadway: Opening Doors |publisher=Broadwayworld.com |date= |accessdate=2013-10-04}}</ref> Multi-Media Musicals, East West Players Anniversary, MADD, Bay Area Kid Fest. She is a featured singer on the CD, ''Kabaret for Kids''.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://cdbaby.com/cd/ssamuels |title=Samantha Samuels | KABARET FOR KIDS | CD Baby Music Store |publisher=Cdbaby.com |date= |accessdate=2013-10-04}}</ref>

Oda has been performing in professional theatre since the age of six. Shows include The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Casting_Announced_For_San_Jose_Repertorys_Production_Of_THE_25TH_ANNUAL_PUTNAM_COUNTY_SPELLING_BEE_20090503 |title=Casting Announced For San Jose Repertory's Production Of THE 25TH ANNUAL PUTNAM COUNTY SPELLING BEE |publisher=Broadwayworld.com |date= |accessdate=2013-10-04}}</ref> the world premiere of ''A Little Princess'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://broadwayworld.com/bwidb/productions/A_Little_Princess_5671 |title=A Little Princess - 2004 Regional (US) |publisher=Broadwayworld.com |date= |accessdate=2013-10-04}}</ref> the West Coast premiere of ''Jane Eyre: the Musical'', ''The Sound of Music'', ''Pacific Overtures'', ''Annie'', ''The Joy Luck Club'', ''A Midsummer Night's Dream'', ''South Pacific'', ''The King and I'' and more.

Oda graduated from the [[University of California, Irvine]] in 2012 with a B.F.A in Musical Theatre.<ref name=Resume>{{cite web|title=Resume|url=http://www.sophieoda.com/Sophie_Oda/Resume.html|publisher=Sophieoda.com|accessdate=2013-10-04}}</ref>

==Career==
Oda had a recurring role in ''[[The Suite Life of Zack & Cody]]'' as [[The Suite Life of Zack & Cody recurring characters#Barbara|Barbara Brownstein]]. She appeared in two movies: ''[[Bee Season (film)|Bee Season]]'' and ''[[Kung Phooey]]''. Oda has been a singer on ''[[Star Search]]''. She has been a guest star in the latest sitcom, ''[[The Suite Life on Deck]]'', with her recurring role as Barbara. Oda is starring in a comedy [[web series]] called ''Spaz Fu''.<ref>[http://www.spazfu.com/SpazFu/Welcome.html]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090510071027/http://www.spazfu.com/SpazFu/Welcome.html|date=May 10, 2009}}</ref>

'''Julián López de Lerma Barahona''' (born 27 February 1987) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]]. He is the current [[Manager (association football)|manager]] of [[Primera Federación]] club [[Real Madrid Castilla]].

==Playing career==
López was born in [[Badajoz]], [[Extremadura]]. After graduating from [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]]'s youth system, he made his first-team debut in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], playing seven [[La Liga]] matches mostly always as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] (he was initially summoned for the [[2007 UEFA Cup final]] against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], but eventually did not make the final list of 18). For the [[2007–08 Segunda División|following season]], he was loaned to [[Sevilla Atlético]] in the [[Segunda División]], appearing rarely due to a severe injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/recreativo-espanyol-cronica-239434/0/|title=Tamudo fulmina el sueño europeo del Recreativo en el Nuevo Colombino (0–1)|trans-title=Tamudo obliterates Recreativo's European dream at the Nuevo Colombino (0–1)|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=27 May 2007|access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref><ref name=Crack>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/espanyol/20110804/julian-crack-que-las-lesiones-retiraron/1105692.shtml|title=Julián, el crack al que las lesiones retiraron|trans-title=Julián, a star finished by injuries|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=Jordi|last=Luengo|language=es|date=4 August 2011|access-date=16 March 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112193041/http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/espanyol/20110804/julian-crack-que-las-lesiones-retiraron/1105692.shtml|archive-date=12 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sevillismoenvena.com/2015/11/que-fue-de-los-integrantes-del-sevilla.html|title=¿Qué fue de los integrantes del Sevilla Atlético de Segunda división?|trans-title=What happened to members of Sevilla Atlético of ''Segunda división''?|publisher=Sevillismo en Vena|language=es|date=5 November 2015|access-date=29 May 2019}}</ref>

In January 2009, having made no competitive appearances for the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] during the first half of [[2008–09 La Liga|the campaign]], López served another loan, now with Greek side [[Panthrakikos F.C.|Panthrakikos]], and again suffered a physical setback, fracturing his right leg. After returning to the [[RCDE Stadium]], whilst training with [[RCD Espanyol B|the reserves]], he was again seriously injured.<ref name=Crack/>

On 3 March 2011, following a failed move to [[CF Gavà|Gavà]], López terminated his contract and signed with amateurs [[UE Rubí|Rubí]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fuerzaperica.com/julian_lopez_de_lerma_ficha_por_el_rubi-itemap-69-30425-1.htm|title=Julian Lopez de Lerma ficha por el Rubi|trans-title=Julian Lopez de Lerma signs for Rubí|publisher=Fuerza Perica|language=es|date=3 March 2011|access-date=16 March 2012}}</ref> In July, aged only 24, he retired from football due to his constant problems with injuries.<ref name=Crack/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoy.es/v/20110723/deportes/futbol/julian-lopez-lerma-cuelga-20110723.html|title=Julián López de Lerma cuelga las botas|trans-title=Julián López de Lerma hangs up boots|newspaper=[[Hoy (Extremadura)|Hoy]]|first=M.|last=Pérez|language=es|date=23 July 2011|access-date=16 March 2012}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
López returned to his main club Espanyol in early November 2011, working as [[Scout (sport)|scout]] in its academy.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/espanyol/julian-vuelve-espanyol-como-parte-del-organigrama-del-futbol-base-1207662|title=Julián vuelve al Espanyol como parte del organigrama del fútbol base|trans-title=Julián returns to Espanyol as part of youth football structure|newspaper=Sport|language=es|date=4 November 2011|access-date=16 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elperiodico.com/es/noticias/deportes/espanyol-ficha-julian-para-futbol-base-1207690|title=El Espanyol recupera al canterano Julián para el fútbol base|trans-title=Espanyol rescue youth player Julián to youth football|newspaper=[[El Periódico (Barcelona)|El Periódico]]|first=Juan|last=Terrats|language=es|date=4 November 2011|access-date=16 March 2012}}</ref> He became manager of their youth sides the following year, before joining [[Manolo González]]'s staff at the reserves in July 2023 as assistant.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/es/noticia/ya-se-conoce-el-cuerpo-tecnico-del-espanyol-b/15762|title=Ya se conoce el cuerpo técnico del Espanyol B|trans-title=The technical staff of Espanyol B is already known|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=es|date=11 July 2023|accessdate=13 January 2026}}</ref>

In July 2024, López moved to the structure of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], being appointed at the ''Juvenil B'' squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.relevo.com/futbol/liga-primera/real-madrid-lleva-espanyol-entrenar-20240708204519-nt.html|title=El Real Madrid se lleva a un ex del Espanyol para entrenar en La Fábrica|trans-title=Real Madrid bring in a former Espanyol man to manage in The Factory|publisher=[[Relevo]]|first=Rodra|last=P.|language=es|date=8 July 2024|access-date=13 January 2026}}</ref> He took over the A team one year later,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/futbol/cantera-masculina/actualidad/el-juvenil-a-inicio-la-pretemporada-30-07-2025|title=Los tres equipos juveniles ya preparan la temporada 2025/26|trans-title=The three ''Juvenil'' teams already prepare for the 2025/26 season|publisher=Real Madrid CF|language=es|date=30 July 2025|access-date=13 January 2026}}</ref> and became head coach of the [[Real Madrid Castilla|senior reserves]] in the [[Primera Federación]] on 14 January 2026 after [[Álvaro Arbeloa]] was promoted to the main squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/academy/latest-news/primer-dia-de-trabajo-de-julian-lopez-de-lerma-al-frente-del-castilla-14-01-2026|title=Julián López de Lerma takes charge of first Castilla training session|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=14 January 2026|access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://okdiario.com/diariomadridista/real-madrid/nuevo-entrenador-del-castilla-elogia-arbeloa-entrenador-fantastico-hecho-trabajazo-598538|title=El nuevo entrenador del Castilla elogia a Arbeloa: «Es un entrenador fantástico y ha hecho un trabajazo»|trans-title=The new Castilla manager praises Arbeloa: "He's a fantastic manager and he has done one hell of a job"|newspaper=[[Okdiario]]|first=Luis|last=Cobos|language=es|date=18 January 2026|access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Amber Dawn Stevens West''' (born October 7, 1986)<ref name="asw.com"/> is an American actress. She is known for her roles as Ashleigh Howard in the [[Freeform (TV channel)|ABC Family]] series ''[[Greek (TV series)|Greek]]'' (2007–2011)'',''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tvovermind.com/five-things-didnt-know-amber-stevens-west/|title=Five Things You Didn't Know about Amber Stevens West|last=Nat|date=2017-06-12|website=TVOvermind|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-13}}</ref> Maxine in the [[NBC]] sitcom ''[[The Carmichael Show]]'' (2015–2017),<ref name="KTLA-CarmichaelShow-2015">{{cite news|last1=Rubin|first1=Sam|title=Amber Stevens West Talks 'The Carmichael Show'|url=http://ktla.com/2015/08/26/amber-stevens-west-talks-the-carmichael-show/|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=[[KTLA Morning News]]|date=August 26, 2015}}</ref> and Claire Davis in the [[CBS]] comedy ''[[Happy Together (American TV series)|Happy Together]]'' (2018–2019). She has also appeared in films ''[[The Amazing Spider-Man (2012 film)|The Amazing Spider-Man]]'' (2012), ''[[22 Jump Street]]'' (2014) and ''[[Jessabelle]]'' (2014). She played the lead role of Maya in the 2018 comedy film ''[[Love Jacked]]''.

== Early life ==
Stevens West was born Amber Dawn Stevens in [[Los Angeles]], California, the daughter of former model Beverly Cunningham and radio announcer [[Shadoe Stevens]].<ref name="asw.com">{{cite web|url=http://amberstevenswest.com/biography|title=Amber Stevens West Biography|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116221229/http://amberstevenswest.com/biography|archive-date=January 16, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has a younger sister named Chyna and an older paternal half-brother named Brad.<ref name=HuffPo-ShadoeSober-2014>{{cite news|title=Former 'American Top 40' Host Shadoe Stevens On Celebrating 30 Years Of Sobriety|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/10/17/shadoe-stevens-celebrates-sobriety_n_5999800.html|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=[[Huffington Post]]|date=October 17, 2014}}</ref> Stevens is of mixed ethnicity, being born to a white father and African-American mother<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://yourblackworld.net/2017/06/26/7-quick-facts-to-know-about-actress-model-amber-stevens-west/|title=7 Quick Facts to Know About Actress & Model Amber Stevens West|date=2017-06-26|website=Your Black World|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-13}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> who is also part [[Comanche]].<ref name=SwirlGirlArmy-Icon-2014>{{cite news|title=Swirl Girl Icon: Amber Stevens!|url=http://swirlgirlarmy.com/post/60852705671/swirl-girl-icon-amber-stevens|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=Swirl Girl Army|date=2014}}</ref><ref name=SheKnows-Ethnicity-2015>{{cite news|last1=Carlbert|first1=Michelle|title=Interview: Amber Stevens on how her ethnicity has affected her career|url=http://www.sheknows.com/entertainment/articles/1093923/the-carmichael-show-amber-stevens-west-interview|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=SheKnows|date=August 26, 2015}}</ref>

Stevens West is a graduate of [[Beverly Hills High School]].<ref name=VanityFair-Sitcom-2014>{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Krista|title=Amber Stevens Would Like to Work on a Sitcom|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2014/08/amber-stevens-actress-photos|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|date=September 2014}}</ref>

==Career==
Early in her career, she appeared in television commercials for [[Old Navy]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brainyquote.com/quotes/amber_stevens_556598|title=Amber Stevens Quotes|website=BrainyQuote|language=en|access-date=2019-09-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://motivationquotes.org/quotes/1567787205686|title=Amber Stevens Quotes|access-date=1 June 2020|publisher=MotivationQuotes}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> [[Verizon Communications|Verizon]], [[Logitech]] and [[Neutrogena]]. She made her television acting debut in an episode of ''[[Complete Savages]]'' in 2005. In 2007, Stevens West began portraying Ashleigh Howard on the [[Freeform (TV channel)|ABC Family]] comedy-drama television series ''[[Greek (TV series)|Greek]]''.<ref name=About-Greek-2012>{{cite web|last1=Thomas|first1=Rachel|url=http://tvdramas.about.com/od/greek/a/amberstevenint.htm|title=An Interview with Amber Stevens (Ashleigh, Greek)|work=About Entertainment|date=August 1, "captures the spirit of the hedge-fund age like nothing else."<ref name="post-gazette">{{cite web|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07180/795662-352.stm|title=Freaks and Greeks|date=June 29, Up!]]'' (2009), ''[[The Amazing Spider-Man (2012 film)|The Amazing Spider-Man]]'' (2012), ''[[The Kitchen (2012 film)|The Kitchen]]'' (2012) and ''[[Jessabelle]]'' (2014).

She has appeared in guest roles on ''[[How I Met Your Mother]]'', ''[[Friends with Benefits (TV series)|Friends with Benefits]]'', ''[[Baby Daddy]]'', ''[[90210 (TV series)|90210]]'', ''[[Ben and Kate]]'' and ''[[New Girl]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/amber-stevens-west/credits/832324|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150909001251/http://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/amber-stevens-west/credits/832324/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 9, 2015|title=Amber Stevens West {{!}} TV Guide|website=TVGuide.com|language=en|access-date=2019-09-13}}</ref> In 2011, Stevens West played the role of Mimi Marquez in the musical ''Rent: Downtown L.A.''<ref name=LADowntown->{{cite web|last1=Chen|first1=Roselle|url=http://www.ladowntownnews.com/entertainment/article_c772dcea-e8bc-53c9-8e31-ecab79e10430.html|title=Hey Kids, Let's Put on a Secret Show|work=Los Angeles Downtown News|date=April 29, 2011|access-date=August 16, 2012}}</ref> She made a guest appearance as Joy Struthers on [[CBS]]' ''[[Criminal Minds]]'', in the episode "Fate". In 2014, she appeared as [[Jonah Hill]]'s character's love interest called Maya in the comedy film ''[[22 Jump Street]].''<ref name=BlackFilm-22JumpSt-2014>{{cite news|last1=Morales|first1=Wilson|title=Exclusive: Amber Stevens Talks '22 Jump Street'|url=http://www.blackfilm.com/read/2014/06/exclusive-amber-stevens-talks-22-jump-street/|access-date=March 14, 2016|work=Black Film|date=June 16, 2014|archive-date=January 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118032208/http://www.blackfilm.com/read/2014/06/exclusive-amber-stevens-talks-22-jump-street/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2015, Stevens West co-starred opposite [[Jerrod Carmichael]] as Maxine in the [[NBC]] comedy sitcom ''[[The Carmichael Show]].''<ref name=KTLA-CarmichaelShow-2015 /> In 2017, following that show's end, Stevens West was cast as a series regular on the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|FOX]] supernatural comedy series ''[[Ghosted (TV series)|Ghosted]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/07/ghosted-amber-stevens-west-cast-carmichael-show-recasting-fox-comedy-series-1202127126/|title='Ghosted' Fox Comedy Adds 'Carmichael Show's Amber Stevens West In Recasting|publisher=Deadline|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=July 12, 2017|access-date=July 12, 2017}}</ref> She portrayed a restaurant and bar designer Claire Davis opposite [[Damon Wayans Jr.]] on [[CBS]]' comedy television series ''[[Happy Together (American TV series)|Happy Together]]'' (2018–2019).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/10/01/entertainment/amber-west-stevens-happy-together/index.html|title=Amber Stevens West was happy to break pregnancy stigmas on 'Happy Together' set|author=Sandra Gonzalez|website=CNN|date=October 2018|access-date=2019-09-14}}</ref> The series followed a young couple whose lives are suddenly thrown into chaos when a pop star moves into their home.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://nypost.com/2018/09/28/amber-stevens-west-says-happy-together-got-creative-hiding-her-baby-bump/|title=Amber Stevens West says 'Happy Together' got creative hiding her baby bump|date=2018-09-29|work=New York Post|access-date=2019-09-14|language=en-US}}</ref>

In May 2021, Stevens starred as one of the four leads in the first season of the ensemble comedy ''[[Run the World (TV series)|Run the World]]'' on [[Starz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amber Stevens West Grew Up in a 'Beautiful Existence' Where 'Race Wasn't Really Discussed' — but Now Is Ready to Talk |url=https://people.com/human-interest/amber-stevens-west-on-black-representation-in-media/ |access-date=2023-11-29 |website=Peoplemag |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2022, Stevens was a contestant on the daytime game show, ''[[Pictionary (2022 game show)|Pictionary]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CjO3wm2uT9j/|title=PictionaryonTV on Instagram: "MONDAY! [[Avex Group|Avex]] (Japan only, 2007–2009) | website = {{URL|https://www.facebook.com/TeamAksent/}} }} '''Krystle Kantrece Johnson''' (born May 29, 1987), better known by her stage name '''Ak'Sent''', is an American rapper. She is from [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. ==Early life and career== Ak'Sent grew up quickly thanks to a rough childhood.[http://www.aksent.com/bio.asp Biography]{{Cite web |url=http://www.djbooth.net/index/interviews/entry/aksent-interview/ |title=Ak'Sent Interview |access-date=2009-09-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080830075719/http://www.djbooth.net/index/interviews/entry/aksent-interview/ |archive-date=2008-08-30 |url-status=dead }} Her father was an aspiring rapper caught up in the gang lifestyle and was killed in a gang shooting when she was four years old, and with her mother unable to support her on her own, she was sent to live with her grandparents in [[South Central, Los Angeles]]. Ak'Sent was signed to [[Capitol Records]] when she was only 16. Since then she has worked with a number of well-known professionals such as The Jugganauts, [[DJ Quik]], & [[Beenie Man]].{{AllMusic|class=album|id=r828466|pure_url=yes}} Ak'Sent aims to avoid the glorification of violence and prefers to think of [[Hip-Hop]] as a form of "street poetry."Aksent Song Review at raphiphopmusic dot com Her first album, ''International'', was released on September 26, 2006. She released her second album ''Gem-In-I'' under the Avex label.{{Cite web|url=http://www.cdjapan.co.jp/detailview.html?KEY=AVCD-23626|title = GEM-IN-I Ak'SenT CD Album|website = CDJapan}} It was released on July 16, 2008 in [[Japan]] only. She is currently recording her third album and a mixtape. ===Behind the music=== Although Ak'Sent signed to a major label when she was only 16 years old. Adding to her challenges, rap music wasn't allowed in her grandparents' house, but as Ak'Sent learned more about her father's hip-hop aspirations, she decided she should carry on in his honor. She eventually spent time in several R&B-based girl groups and began dance training with Debbie Allen. One showcase at the age of 16 had the young multi-talent signed to Capitol and working with the production duo The Jugganauts. Ak'Sent was especially excited about the Caribbean-styled beats the Jugganauts were working on, and soon she was writing a series of dancehall numbers. {{short description|Australian actor (born 1985)}} {{Other people}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2022}} {{Infobox person |name = Luke Mitchell |image = Luke Mitchell by Gage Skidmore.jpg |imagesize = |caption = Mitchell in 2016 |years_active = 2008–present |occupation = Actor |birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1985|4|17|df=yes}} |birth_place = [[Gold Coast, Queensland]], Australia |spouse = {{marriage|[[Rebecca Breeds]]|2013}} |children = 1 }} '''Luke Mitchell''' (born 17 April 1985) is an Australian actor. He attended the Film and Television Studio International, and won the role of [[Chris Knight (Neighbours)|Chris Knight]] in ''[[Neighbours]]'' in 2008. Mitchell appeared as Will in the third season of ''[[H2O: Just Add Water|H2O: Just Add Water]]'' in 2009. He starred as [[Romeo Smith]] in ''[[Home and Away]]'' from 2009 to 2013. The role saw Mitchell win the Most Popular New Male Talent [[Logie Award]] in 2010. In 2013, he starred as John Young in the CW's ''[[The Tomorrow People (American TV series)|The Tomorrow People]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-cw-renewed-cancelled-series-2014-the-carrie-diaries-514943/|title='Carrie Diaries,' 'Tomorrow People' Cancelled, 'Dixie,' 'Beauty' Renewed by The CW|first=Michael|last=Slezak|date=8 May 2014|work=TVLine|access-date=23 August 2014|archive-date=8 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508223516/http://tvline.com/2014/05/08/the-cw-renewed-cancelled-series-2014-the-carrie-diaries/|url-status=live}} In 2015, he joined the cast of ''[[Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.]]'' for the series' second season, playing the recurring character of [[Inhumans (Marvel Cinematic Universe)|Inhuman]] [[Lincoln Campbell]], before being promoted to series regular for its third season. He joined NBC's ''[[Blindspot (TV series)|Blindspot]]'' as a series regular during its second season in 2016, playing Roman. ==Early life== Mitchell was born on 17 April 1985 and grew up on the [[Gold Coast, Queensland|Gold Coast]].{{cite journal|last=Chegwidden|first=Yvette|date=5–11 September 2009|title=New boy in the Bay|journal=[[TV Week]]|issue=36|page=17}} His parents later divorced and both went on to remarry. Mitchell has three brothers, Michael, Daniel and Benjamin and a younger sister, Bree. His older brother coaches tennis, while his younger brother, [[Benjamin Mitchell (tennis)|Ben]], was in the top 10 of Australian Tennis Players and peaked at 109 in the world rankings. Mitchell played tennis from the age of five to nineteen. He aimed to go professional, but gave it up after realizing it was the only thing in his life. Mitchell attended [[Nerang State High School]]. ==Career== Mitchell trained at the Film and Television Studio International and worked with professionals such as Joss McWilliam, Iain Gardner, Kim Krejus and Dean Carey. He travelled around Australia with international entertainment company [[Sudden Impact Entertainment]] and worked in their live theatre shows. Whilst working in [[Melbourne]] he successfully auditioned for the guest-role of [[Chris Knight (Neighbours)|Chris Knight]] in ''[[Neighbours]]'' and appeared in 11 episodes. He then moved back to the Gold Coast to play the part of Will in the third season of ''[[H2O: Just Add Water|H2O: Just Add Water]]''. In 2008, Mitchell filmed the gay-themed romance ''Performance Anxiety'', which was selected as part of the 9th Annual Brisbane Queer Film Festival as a screening for cast and crew. In June 2009, Mitchell relocated to [[Sydney]] and began starring as [[Romeo Smith]] in ''[[Home and Away]]''. Mitchell won the 2010 [[Logie Award]] for Most Popular New Male Talent for his portrayal of Romeo. On 4 November 2012, it was announced that Mitchell had chosen to leave ''Home and Away'' after four years and his character departed on-screen in 2013. '''Teala Dunn''' (born December 8, 1996)<ref>{{cite web |title=Teala Dunn's official TikTok |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@ttlyteala/video/7446227259452607774?lang=en |access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2021/12/08/horoscopes-dec-8-2021-ian-somerhalder-refuse-to-let-anyone-discourage-you/|title=Horoscopes Dec. 8, 2021: Ian Somerhalder, refuse to let anyone discourage you|first=Eugenia|last=Last|date=December 8, 2021|access-date=July 12, 2026}}</ref> is an American actress and [[YouTuber]]. She is best known for voicing Tuck on ''[[Wonder Pets!]]''. She also played Lindsey Persons in the TBS sitcom ''[[Are We There Yet? (TV series)|Are We There Yet?]]''.

==Career==
Teala Dunn is known for her role as a YouTube vlogger, and she is also known for her recurring role as Juanita on the [[Nickelodeon]] television show ''[[The Naked Brothers Band (TV series)|The Naked Brothers Band]]'', Kelsey on ''[[The Thundermans]]'', and as the voice of the turtle Tuck in ''[[Wonder Pets!]].''

Dunn made a guest appearance in ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]''. In film, she was seen in ''[[Phoebe in Wonderland]]'', which premiered at the [[Sundance Film Festival]] in 2008. She also appeared with [[Felicity Huffman]] in ''[[Transamerica (film)|Transamerica]]'', and was also heard as a bunny in Disney's ''[[Enchanted (film)|Enchanted]]''. Dunn appeared on ''[[Shake It Up (American TV series)|Shake It Up]]'' as Dina's childhood nemesis, and also appeared on ''[[Enlisted (TV series)|Enlisted]]'' as Donald Cody's teenage daughter.

Dunn began voicing the superhero [[Bumblebee (DC Comics)|Bumblebee]] in the animated series ''[[DC Super Hero Girls]]'' in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sands |first=Rich |date=2016-02-11 |title='DC Super Hero Girls' Brings New Meaning to the Term Girl Power (VIDEO) |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/72532/dc-super-hero-girls-brings-new-meaning-to-the-term-girl-power-video/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=TV Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> She has continued to voice the character in subsequent films, including ''[[DC Super Hero Girls: Intergalactic Games]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |date=Mar 11, 2017 |title=Class is Back In Session with New DC Super Hero Girls: Intergalactic Games Trailer |url=https://www.freecomicbookday.com/Article/191607-Class-is-Back-In-Session-with-New-DC-Super-Hero-Girls-Intergalactic-Games-Trailer |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=Free Comic Book Day}}</ref> ''[[Lego DC Super Hero Girls: Brain Drain]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ching |first=Albert |date=2017-05-31 |title=EXCLUSIVE: LEGO Meets DC Super Hero Girls in Brain Drain Trailer |url=https://www.cbr.com/lego-dc-super-hero-girls-brain-drain-trailer/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=CBR |language=en}}</ref> ''[[Lego DC Super Hero Girls: Super-Villain High]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jenna |date=2018-02-21 |title='LEGO DC Super Hero Girls: Super-Villain High' Movie to Get May 2018 Release |url=https://comicbook.com/dc/news/lego-dc-super-hero-girls-super-villain-high-trailer-cast/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=ComicBook.com |language=en-US}}</ref> and ''[[DC Super Hero Girls: Legends of Atlantis]].''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aguilar |first=Matthew |date=2018-06-28 |title='DC Super Hero Girls: Legends of Atlantis' Release Date Announced |url=https://comicbook.com/dc/news/dc-super-hero-girls-legends-of-atlantis-release-date/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=ComicBook.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2017, Dunn starred in the [[AT&T]] Hello Lab drama series ''Guilty Party''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2017-08-16 |title=AT&T Hello Lab Casts Digital Influencers for Cyberbullying Social-Media Drama Series 'Guilty Party' |url=https://variety.com/2017/digital/news/att-hello-lab-guilty-party-cyberbullying-drama-1202529719/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> The following year, she collaborated with [[Eva Marie]]'s NEM Fashion brand to launch a limited edition line of sunglasses.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2018 |title=Teala Dunn launches fashion sunglasses with NEM (Natalie's 'Eva Marie' brand) |url=https://teenswannaknow.com/teala-dunn-launches-fashion-sunglasses-with-nem-natalies-eva-marie-brand/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Teens Wanna Know |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2020, she joined the content creator collective Clubhouse BH.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twersky |first=Carolyn |date=2020-07-23 |title=Some New Faces Are Joining The Clubhouse and You're Definitely Going to Recognize Them |url=https://www.seventeen.com/celebrity/a33396200/teala-dunn-the-montes-twins-joining-clubhouse-bh/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Seventeen |language=en-US}}</ref> Dunn later began hosting the [[Spotify|Spotify Original]] podcast ''Adulting with Teala & Nia''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMillian |first=Laurise |title=How Podcast Hosts Teala Dunn and Nia Sioux Are Addressing Microaggressions In The Workplace |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/how-to-deal-with-workplace-microagressions |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Refinery29 |language=en}}</ref>

Dunn appeared as Zelda in the [[Freeform (TV channel)|Freeform]] series ''[[Good Trouble (TV series)|Good Trouble]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2022 |title=From “Crush” to “Good Trouble”: An Interview with Teala Dunn |url=https://www.thecherrypicks.com/stories/from-crush-to-good-trouble-an-interview-with-teala-dunn |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=CherryPicks}}</ref> In 2022, she hosted the [[Brat TV]] podcast ''Anonymously Yours''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hale |first=James |date=2022-07-04 |title=Teala Dunn takes fans' confessions in new podcast 'Anonymously Yours' (Exclusive) |url=https://www.tubefilter.com/2022/07/04/teala-dunn-anonymously-yours-youtube-podcast/ |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=Tubefilter |language=en-US}}</ref> She appeared in the [[Hulu]] romantic comedy ''[[Crush (2022 film)|Crush]]'', which premiered that same year.<ref name="Shoot">{{cite web |last1=Herbert |first1=Geoff |date=March 30, 2022 |title=''Crush'' movie: First look at American High's queer teen rom-com shot in Syracuse |url=https://www.syracuse.com/entertainment/2022/03/crush-movie-first-look-at-american-highs-queer-teen-rom-com-shot-in-syracuse.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428223023/https://www.syracuse.com/entertainment/2022/03/crush-movie-first-look-at-american-highs-queer-teen-rom-com-shot-in-syracuse.html |archive-date=April 28, 2022 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=[[Syracuse.com]]}}</ref> She appeared in the musical film ''[[Rockbottom]]'' in 2024,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/jake-bongiovi-hair-band-movie-rockbottom-1235521962|website=Variety|date=February 16, 2023|title=Jake Bongiovi Joins Tom Everett Scott in Hair Band Comedy 'Rockbottom' (EXCLUSIVE)|first=Matt|last=Donnelly|accessdate=April 11, 2023}}</ref> and the horror film ''[[Werewolf Game]]'' in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Complex |first=Valerie |date=2022-03-22 |title=Lydia Hearst Joins Cast Of New Social Media Themed Horror Film ''Werewolf Game'' |url=https://deadline.com/2022/03/lydia-hearst-joins-cast-of-new-social-media-horror-werewolf-game-1234983830/ |access-date=2024-08-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> Dunn also launched a beauty brand titled Creme de la Cube.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=D'Shonda |date=2024-05-01 |title=Teala Dunn Doesn't Think There's A Such Thing As Too Many Celebrity Skincare Lines |url=https://girlsunited.essence.com/feedback/news/teala-dunn-interview-skincare/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Girls United |language=en-US}}</ref> She is set to appear in the [[Tom Arnold (actor)|Tom Arnold]]'s directorial debut ''The Breakup Pill'', a high-concept romantic comedy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=2025-10-17 |title=Tom Arnold Wraps On Feature Directorial Debut 'The Breakup Pill' – First Look |url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/tom-arnold-directs-the-breakup-pill-stars-mcabe-gregg-teala-dunn-1236590566/ |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Dunn lives in Los Angeles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manoff |first=Jill |date=2019-06-06 |title=5 Gen-Z influencers you need to know |url=https://digiday.com/marketing/5-gen-z-influencers-know/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Digiday |language=en-US}}</ref> She has an older sister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comiskey |first=Michael |last2=Lin |first2=Joselyn |last3=Martinez |first3=Emily |last4=Morrison |first4=Amanda |date=2011-07-31 |title=Kidsday talks with actress Teala Dunn |url=https://www.newsday.com/lifestyle/family/kidsday-talks-with-actress-teala-dunn-o62069 |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Newsday |language=en}}</ref>

'''Samantha Harper''' (née '''Boscarino'''; born December 26, 1994) is an American actress. She gained early attention for her role in the teen comedy film ''[[The Clique (film)|The Clique]]'' (2008), followed by her recurring role in the [[Disney Channel]] sitcom ''[[Good Luck Charlie]]'' (2010{{ndash}}2014), and her lead roles as Molly Garfunkel on the short-lived [[Nickelodeon]] series ''[[How to Rock]]'' (2012), and Ellie Davis in the 2016 [[television film]] ''The Cheerleader Murders''.

==Career==
Her first notable role was as Alicia Rivera in the film ''[[The Clique (film)|The Clique]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.moviefone.com/movie/the-clique/34085/credits |title=The Clique (2008) Cast & Crew |website=Moviefone |publisher=AOL Inc. |year=2016 |access-date=2016-04-27}}</ref> produced by [[Tyra Banks]], and costarring [[Bridgit Mendler]]. In 2009, she appeared in ''[[The Perfect Game]]'' as Gloria Jimenez and in ''[[Jonas (TV series)|Jonas]]'' as Amy. Boscarino also appeared in ''[[Parenthood (2010 TV series)|Parenthood]]'' as Lindsay and ''[[True Jackson, VP]]'' as Carla Gustav. Boscarino also had a nine-episode recurring role in ''[[Good Luck Charlie]]'' as Skyler, reuniting her with Mendler.<ref>{{cite web |author=Victoria Leigh Miller |url=https://www.yahoo.com/tv/bp/bridgit-mendler-says-goodbye-to--good-luck-charlie----i-ll-really-miss-the-duncans-194616724.html |title=Bridgit Mendler Says Goodbye to 'Good Luck Charlie': 'I'll Really Miss the Duncans' |work=[[Yahoo TV]] |date=February 15, 2014 |access-date=2016-04-15 |quote=But there've been a lot of special guest stars. I loved having my other friends; Samantha Boscarino was on the show.}}</ref>  In mid-2010, she appeared as Lisa Cucuy in ''[[Wizards of Waverly Place]]''. In 2011, she made an appearance on ''[[Bucket & Skinner's Epic Adventures]]'' as C.J.

In 2012, Boscarino was cast as Molly Garfunkel on the [[Nickelodeon]] series ''[[How to Rock]]''.<ref name="THR-HTR">{{cite web |author=Philiana Ng |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/nickelodeon-greenlights-how-rock-series-191135 |title=Nickelodeon Greenlights 'How to Rock' to Series |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=May 23, 2011 |access-date=2016-04-12}}</ref><ref name="V-HTR">{{cite web |author=Brian Lowry |url=https://variety.com/2012/tv/reviews/how-to-rock-1117946998/ |title=Review: 'How to Rock' |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=February 2, 2012 |access-date=2016-04-12 |quote=The opener (part of a back-to-back episode launch) thus focuses on whether Kacey will sing with them in the big talent show against her former mates, Molly (Samantha Boscarino) and Grace (Halston Sage), with whom she loved to pose and shop.}}</ref><ref name="TNYT-HTR">{{cite web |author=Kathryn Shattuck |url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9800E2DE153AF937A35751C0A9649D8B63 |title=What's On Today |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=February 4, 2012 |access-date=2016-04-12 |quote=Samantha Boscarino and Halston Sage are members of the Perfs, her former friends and newest rivals.}}</ref> The series premiered on February 4, 2012,<ref name="V-HTR" /> and ended on December 8, 2012. She made several appearances on ''[[Figure It Out]]'' as a panelist. In 2016, Boscarino was the lead in the [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime]] television film, ''The Cheerleader Murders'', playing the role of Ellie.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mylifetime.com/movies/the-cheerleader-murders |title=The Cheerleader Murders |website=mylifetime.com |access-date=2016-04-12}}</ref><ref name="TCM">{{cite web |author=Ed Stockly |url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/tv/showtracker/la-et-st-saturday-s-tv-highlights-and-weekend-talk-nothing-left-unsaid-gloria-vanderbilt-anderson-cooper-on-h-20160408-story.html |title=Saturday's TV Highlights and Weekend Talk: 'Nothing Left Unsaid: Gloria Vanderbilt & Anderson Cooper' on HBO |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 8, 2016 |access-date=2016-04-12}}</ref>
