'''José Carlos Tofolo Júnior''', commonly known as '''Alemão''' (born 2 March 1989), is a Brazilian [[association football|football]] [[Coach (sport)|coach]] and former player who played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. He is the current head coach of [[Atlético Monte Azul|Monte Azul]].

Alemão also holds Italian nationality.<ref name=eindhoven>{{cite web|url=http://fc-eindhoven.nl/1e-elftal/spelers/jose-carlos-tofolo-junior-alemao|title=José Carlos Tofolo Júnior (Alemão)|date=2016|access-date=27 September 2016|publisher=FC Eindhoven|language=Dutch|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927200223/http://fc-eindhoven.nl/1e-elftal/spelers/jose-carlos-tofolo-junior-alemao|archive-date=27 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Club career==

===Early career===
Alemão started his career at [[Santos FC|Santos]], and signed a professional contract with club in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.uol.com.br/cbf/bide/bid_a.htm|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060529035842/http://www2.uol.com.br/cbf/bide/bid_a.htm|title=BID ACUMULATIVO SÉRIE A /2005|date=8 November 2005|archivedate=29 May 2006|accessdate=6 July 2010|work=Confederação Brasileira de Futebol (CBF)}}</ref> He made his first team debut on 31 January 2008, starting in a 1–2 [[2008 Campeonato Paulista|Campeonato Paulista]] loss against [[Grêmio Recreativo Barueri|Grêmio Barueri]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.futebolpaulista.com.br/sumula_img.php?cat=39&cam=73&jog=50&ano=2008|title=Match Report: Santos 1–2 Grêmio Barueri|date=31 January 2008|accessdate=25 January 2011|work=Federação Paulista de Futebol (FPF)|language=Portuguese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919172503/http://www.futebolpaulista.com.br/sumula_img.php?cat=39&cam=73&jog=50&ano=2008|archive-date=19 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> due to [[Kléber Pereira]]'s injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.santosfc.com.br/noticias/conteudo.asp?id=17565 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718230540/http://www.santosfc.com.br/noticias/conteudo.asp?id=17565 |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 July 2011 |title=Santos FC enfrenta Barueri nesta quinta-feira (31) |date=31 January 2008 |accessdate=25 January 2011 |work=Santos FC |language=Portuguese }}</ref> Alemão scored his first goal for ''Peixe'' four days later, in a 1–1 draw against [[Paulista Futebol Clube|Paulista]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.futebolpaulista.com.br/sumula_img.php?cat=39&cam=73&jog=60&ano=2008|title=Match Report: Paulista 1–1 Santos|date=3 February 2008|accessdate=25 January 2011|work=FPF|language=Portuguese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919172759/http://www.futebolpaulista.com.br/sumula_img.php?cat=39&cam=73&jog=60&ano=2008|archive-date=19 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Udinese/Varese and loans===
In July 2008 he was signed by [[Serie A]] club [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] on a reported free transfer,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Santos/0,,MUL701740-9874,00-ALEMAO+TROCA+A+VILA+PELO+FUTEBOL+ITALIANO.html|title=Alemão troca a Vila pelo futebol italiano|trans-title=Alemão changes ''Vila'' for Italian football|date=26 July 2008|accessdate=25 January 2011|work=GloboEsporte.com|language=Portuguese}}</ref> with performance based fees.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.calcioblog.it/post/6184/udinese-alemao-il-nuovo-kaka-e-in-arrivo|title=Udinese: Alemão, il nuovo Kakà è in arrivo|trans-title=Udinese: Alemão, the new Kaká arrives|date=30 June 2008|accessdate=26 January 2011|work=Calcio Blog|language=Italian}}</ref> However, Alemão was not registered in [[Lega Calcio]] as the club did not have an extra non-EU signing quota (Udinese signed [[Ricardo Chará]], [[Dušan Basta]], [[Alexis Sánchez]] and [[Odion Ighalo]] that season but only the last 2 were officially registered in the League Office). Santos also submitted a new contract to [[Brazilian Football Confederation]] BID-E system to document a new contract which last until 2011 on 28 July. Alemão was only officially signed for Udinese in June 2009, and never appeared for Santos neither in [[2008 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] nor [[2009 Campeonato Paulista]], due to a dispute with the club's board.

With Udinese, Alemão played for its [[Campionato Nazionale Primavera|Primavera under-20 team]] as an overage player.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.udinese.it/ENG/script/view.php?id=171 |title=Udinese Reserves qualify for the round of eight |date=2 May 2010 |accessdate=25 January 2011 |work=Udinese Calcio |publisher=udinese.it |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111201122059/http://udinese.it/ENG/script/view.php?id=171 |archivedate=1 December 2011 }}</ref> In July 2010 he was sold to [[Serie B]] club [[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]] in [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership deal]], for €400,000.<ref>Vicenza Calcio Report and Accounts on 30 June 2011 {{in lang|it}}, [http://www.registroimprese.it/ CCIAA]</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/alemao-biancorosso-cesare-torino |title=Alemao in biancorosso. Di Cesare al Torino |trans-title=Alemão is ''biancorosso''. Di Cesare to Torino |date=16 July 2010 |accessdate=25 January 2011 |work=Vicenza Calcio |language=Italian |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20110125152426/http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/alemao-biancorosso-cesare-torino |archivedate=25 January 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Alemão made his debut abroad on 20 August 2010, [[Substitute (association football)|replacing]] [[Alain Baclet]] in the 66th minute of a 0–2 [[Serie B]] loss against [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/atalanta-vicenza-2-0 |title=Atalanta-Vicenza 2–0 |date=20 August 2010 |accessdate=25 January 2011 |work=Vicenza Calcio |language=Italian }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On 31 January 2011, he was swapped with [[Marco Cellini]] of [[A.S. Varese 1910|Varese]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/arrivano-cellini-morosini-e-frattali-tutte-operazioni |title=Arrivano Cellini, Morosini e Frattali. Tutte le operazioni |trans-title=Arrives Cellini, Morosini and Frattali. All transfers |date=31 January 2011 |work=Vicenza Calcio |language=Italian |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717195525/http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/arrivano-cellini-morosini-e-frattali-tutte-operazioni |archivedate=17 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.varese1910.it/news.php?id=44 |title=Chiuso il mercato: ecco le operazioni ufficiali |trans-title=Transfer market: all the official transfers |date=31 January 2011 |accessdate=8 March 2011 |work=AS Varese 1910 |language=Italian |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722064802/http://www.varese1910.it/news.php?id=44 |archivedate=22 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In June 2011 Udinese gave up the remain 50% registration rights for free.

===Back to Brazil===
In January 2012 Alemão returned to Brazil, signing a temporary deal with [[Grêmio Catanduvense de Futebol|Grêmio Catanduvense]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/alemao-in-prestito-al-gremio-catanduvense/|title=Alemao in prestito al Gremio Catanduvense|date=7 December 2011|access-date=27 September 2016|publisher=Vicenza Calcio|language=Italian|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160930063114/http://www.vicenzacalcio.com/alemao-in-prestito-al-gremio-catanduvense/|archive-date=30 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He moved to [[Guaratinguetá Futebol|Guaratinguetá]] until December in mid-2012.{{citation needed|date=September 2016}} After scoring regularly he moved to neighbouring [[Associação Atlética Ponte Preta|Ponte Preta]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pontepreta.com.br/noticias-detalhe/atacante-alemao-esta-liberado-para-vestir-a-camisa-alvinegra-neste-sabado|title=Atacante Alemão está liberado para vestir a camisa alvinegra neste sábado|date=24 January 2013|access-date=27 September 2016|publisher=Associação Atlética Ponte Preta|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

After only appearing sparingly in [[2013 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2013 Série A]], Alemão was loaned to fellow league team [[Esporte Clube Vitória|Vitória]]. He subsequently was loaned to [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pontepreta.com.br/noticias-detalhe/emprestimos-de-alemao-e-rafael-ratao-sao-oficializados|title=Empréstimos de Alemão e Rafael Ratão são oficializados|date=24 April 2014|access-date=27 September 2016|publisher=Associação Atlética Ponte Preta|language=Portuguese}}</ref> and [[Associação Portuguesa de Desportos|Portuguesa]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pontepreta.com.br/noticias-detalhe/alemao-e-emprestado|title=Alemão é emprestado para a Portuguesa|date=22 August 2014|access-date=27 September 2016|publisher=Associação Atlética Ponte Preta|language=Portuguese}}</ref> in the following year, he scored 8 goals in total in Serie league and State league.

===Cruz Azul===
On 12 December 2014 Alemão signed for [[Liga MX]] side [[Cruz Azul]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/alemao-ex-santos-e-ponte-preta-fecha-com-cruz-azul-do-mexico,5c1d0040b1c3a410VgnCLD200000b2bf46d0RCRD.html|title=Alemão, ex-Santos e Ponte Preta, fecha com Cruz Azul do México|trans-title=Alemão, former Santos and Ponte Preta player, signs with Mexican Cruz Azul|publisher=Terra|language=pt|date=12 December 2014|accessdate=19 December 2014|archive-date=19 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219160905/http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/alemao-ex-santos-e-ponte-preta-fecha-com-cruz-azul-do-mexico,5c1d0040b1c3a410VgnCLD200000b2bf46d0RCRD.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He got 3 goals and 4 assists during 14 games but [[Figueirense]] wants him to play in the club {{citation needed span|text=as loan. |date=September 2016}}

===Second Return to Brazil===
In 2015, he returned to Brazil again for [[Figueirense]]. He then signed by [[ABC Futebol Clube|ABC]] and Ribeirão Preto based [[Botafogo Futebol Clube (SP)|Botafogo-SP]].

===FC Eindhoven===
In 2016, he moved to Europe again for Dutch club [[FC Eindhoven]].<ref name=eindhoven/>

[[Pittsburgh Penguins]] | ntl_team = CAN | draft = 7th overall | draft_team = [[Minnesota Wild]] | draft_year = 2012 | career_start = 2013 | career_end = 2026 }} '''Mathew Dumba''' (born July 25, 1994) is a Canadian former professional [[ice hockey]] [[defenceman]]. Dumba was selected with the seventh overall pick by the [[Minnesota Wild]] in the first round of the [[2012 NHL entry draft]], with whom he spent his first ten seasons. He has also played for the [[Arizona Coyotes]], [[Tampa Bay Lightning]], [[Dallas Stars]], and [[Pittsburgh Penguins]]. Dumba previously played junior with the [[Red Deer Rebels]] and briefly for the [[Portland Winterhawks]] of the [[Western Hockey League]] (WHL). ==Early life== Dumba is of [[Filipino Canadians|Filipino]] (maternal) and [[Romanian Canadians|Romanian]] and [[German Canadians|German]] (paternal) descent.{{cite news |last=Doyle |first=Mike |url=https://www.nhl.com/wild/news/passion-on-ice/c-637886 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170923151802/https://www.nhl.com/wild/news/passion-on-ice/c-637886 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 23, 2017 |title=Passion On Ice |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |date=2014-07-14 |access-date=2014-09-21}} He was born in [[Regina, Saskatchewan|Regina]], Saskatchewan, and learned to skate at age three.{{cite news |last=Edmonds |first=Scott |url=http://www.globaltoronto.com/sports/red+deer+rebels+mathew+dumba+captains+canada+at+under-18+world+championship/6442620485/story.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216035551/http://www.globaltoronto.com/sports/red+deer+rebels+mathew+dumba+captains+canada+at+under-18+world+championship/6442620485/story.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |title=Red Deer Rebels' Mathew Dumba captains Canada at under-18 world championship |work=[[Global News]] Toronto |date=2012-04-13 |access-date=2013-01-20}} His family later moved to [[Calgary]], Alberta, where he played his [[minor hockey]] in Calgary with the Crowchild Minor Hockey Association.{{cite journal |last=Potenteau |first=Doyle |title=Defensive Posture |journal=Prospects Hockey |date=Spring 2012 |pages=WHL2–7}} Dumba spent the 2009–10 season with the [[Edge School|Edge School for Athletes]] in the Canadian Sport School Hockey League.{{cite web |url=http://www.csshl.ca/leagues/custom_page.cfm?clientID=4542&leagueID=15269&pageid=14613 |title=Canadian Sport School Hockey League (Design, Hosting, Registration & Administration tools by |archive-date=2013-07-16}} ==Playing career== ===Amateur=== The [[Red Deer Rebels]] of the [[Western Hockey League]] (WHL) selected Dumba with their first-round selection, fourth overall, in the 2009 WHL Bantam Draft from the Calgary Bronks AAA Organization.{{Cite journal|editor=Flett, Cory |editor2=Watts, Jessie|title=2008–09 WHL Guide|journal=Prospects Hockey|publisher=[[Western Hockey League]] |issn=1703-7182 |page=104}} He made his WHL debut in [[2009–10 WHL season|2009–10]], his 15-year-old season, appearing in six regular season games and two playoff games for the Rebels. Joining the Rebels full-time in [[2010–11 WHL season|2010–11]], Dumba scored 15 goals and 26 points and was a player whom his coach said was noticeable every time he was on the ice. His performance during the season earned Dumba the [[Jim Piggott Memorial Trophy]] as the WHL's rookie-of-the-year.{{cite web |last=Morreale |first=Mike G. |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=597591 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216131349/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=597591 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |title=Top WHL draft prospects coming from the blue line |publisher=National Hockey League |date=2011-10-27 |access-date=2013-01-20}} Returning to the Rebels for the [[2011–12 WHL season]], Dumba scored 20 goals and 57 points in 69 games. He was the youngest player invited to the selection camp for the [[2012 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2012 World Junior Hockey Championship]], however he failed to make the team.{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/7-players-cut-from-canada-s-world-junior-squad-1.1046375 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130219191222/http://www.cbc.ca/sports/story/2011/12/13/sp-hockey-canada-world-junior-cuts.html |url-status=live |archive-date=February 19, 2013 |title=7 players cut from Canada's world junior squad |work=CBC Sports |date=2011-12-13 |access-date=2013-01-20}} However, he continued to impress scouts and observers with his play. [[Don Hay]] was one of several WHL coaches to praise Dumba for his enthusiasm on the ice and hard-[[Checking (ice hockey)|checking]] style: "He's a guy who can do all aspects of the game ... he's a very dynamic player with or without the puck. Yes, he can lay out a good bodycheck, but he can also score the overtime winning goal." Dumba's play in the WHL resulted in him being rated as one of the top prospects for the [[2012 NHL entry draft]]. [[NHL Central Scouting Bureau|NHL Central Scouting]] ranked him as the 11th best prospect for the draft, while International Scouting Services ranked him 5th overall.{{cite news |last=Hall |first=Vicki |title=Day of destiny |work=[[Calgary Herald]] |date=2012-06-20 |page=C1}} The [[Minnesota Wild]] selected him in the first round, seventh overall,{{cite news |last=Cruickshank |first=Scott |title=Wild night for local Dumba |work=[[Calgary Herald]] |date=2012-06-23 |page=E1}} and signed him to an NHL contract a month later.{{cite web |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=638258 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216134336/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=638258 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |title=Wild sign teen Matt Dumba, their first round pick |publisher=National Hockey League |date=2012-07-19 |access-date=2013-01-20}} Dumba was returned to the Rebels to begin the [[2012–13 WHL season]], in part due to a [[2012–13 NHL lockout|labour dispute]] between the NHL and its players. When the NHL's dispute was resolved, the Wild intended to give him a brief look at their training camp. Dumba impressed the team's coaching staff enough to earn a spot on the Wild's opening-night roster,{{cite news |last=Goessling |first=Ben |url=http://www.twincities.com/sports/ci_22395306/minnesota-wild-top-pick-matt-dumba-apparently-makes |title=Minnesota Wild: Matt Dumba, 18, earns a roster spot, for now |work=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |date=2013-01-17 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2013-01-20}} however, he was returned to Red Deer four games into the NHL season without having played with the Wild.{{cite news |last=Korac |first=Louie |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/blogpost.htm?id=13375 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216132330/http://www.nhl.com/ice/blogpost.htm?id=13375 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2013 |title=Wild sending Dumba back to Red Deer |publisher=National Hockey League |date=2013-01-27 |access-date=2013-01-27}} ===Professional=== ====Minnesota Wild==== Dumba earned a spot in the Wild lineup to start the [[2013–14 NHL season|2013–14 season]] and made his NHL debut on October 5, 2013, against the [[Anaheim Ducks]], becoming the second player of Filipino descent to play in the NHL, after [[Tim Stapleton]].{{Cite news |title=Flashback: Stars prospect Jason Robertson hasn't forgotten his roots while forging his own NHL path |first=Matthew |last=DeFranks |date=2022-04-27 |orig-date=2019-08-04 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/stars/2019/08/04/stars-prospect-jason-robertson-hasn-t-forgotten-his-roots-while-forging-own-nhl-path/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-07-02}} He scored his first NHL goal on October 12 against [[Dan Ellis (ice hockey)|Dan Ellis]] of the [[Dallas Stars]].{{cite news |title=Rookies Fontaine, Dumba lead Wild past Stars, 5–1 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=2013-10-12 |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=400484315 |access-date=2024-07-02}} He recorded only two points in 13 games by December and the Wild loaned Dumba to the Canadian junior team for the [[2014 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]]. While Dumba was with the national team, the Rebels traded his WHL rights to the [[Portland Winterhawks]] and the Wild assigned him to Portland upon his return from the World Junior Championship.{{cite news |last=Odom |first=Joel |title=Mathew Dumba to join Portland Winterhawks |work=[[The Oregonian]] |date=2014-01-07 |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/hawks/index.ssf/2014/01/mathew_dumba_to_join_portland.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2014-01-07}} In the 2015–16 season, Dumba had a breakout year, playing every game but one with the Minnesota Wild, seeing career highs in goals, assists, points, and penalty minutes with 10 goals, 16 assists, 26 points and 38 PIMS. The Wild also played an outdoor game against the [[Chicago Blackhawks]] at [[TCF Bank Stadium]] as part of the NHL Stadium Series. Dumba got the scoring going early as he trailed the play after [[Ryan Carter]] had a breakaway, Carter had his shot saved and his rebound saved as well but Dumba poked in the third chance for his ninth goal of the season to give the Wild a 1–0 lead.{{cite news |title=NHL outdoor game: Wild crush Blackhawks at TCF Bank Stadium |work=[[CBC Sports]] |last=Campbell |first=Dan |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 21, 2016 |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/stadium-series-minnesota-wild-1.3457892 |access-date=November 20, 2023}} The Wild went on to beat the Blackhawks 6–1. He played 81 out of the 82 games that season, missing only a 3–0 loss to the [[San Jose Sharks]] as a healthy scratch by coach [[John Torchetti]].{{cite news |title=Dumba healthy scratched as Wild look to clinch playoff spot |first=Mike |last=Halford |date=April 5, 2016 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/dumba-healthy-scratched-as-wild-look-to-clinch-playoff-spot |access-date=November 20, 2023}} On July 28, 2016, he re-signed to a two-year, $5.1M bridge deal with the Wild.{{cite web |url=http://wild.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=890302 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160730183745/http://wild.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=890302 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 30, 2016 |title= Wild Agrees To Terms With Matt Dumba On A Two-Year Contract | publisher= Minnesota Wild |date=2016-07-28 |access-date=2016-07-28}} After not getting off to a good start for the Wild, new head coach [[Bruce Boudreau]] opted to scratch Dumba on October 20 against the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]]. The plan was foiled, however, when [[Marco Scandella]] became sick, forcing Dumba into the lineup. After that he played alongside All-Star defenseman [[Ryan Suter]] on the first defensive pairing and saw increased responsibilities and ice time. He averaged 21:48 per game alongside Suter. His [[2017–18 NHL season|2017–18 season]] saw Dumba set new personal bests with 14 goals, 36 assists, and 50 points. On July 21, 2018, Dumba signed a five-year, $30 million contract extension with the Wild, carrying an annual average of $6 million.{{cite magazine |title=Wild Sign Defenseman Matt Dumba to Five-Year, $30 Million Contract |first=Michael |last=Blinn |date=July 21, 2018 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/nhl/2018/07/21/matt-dumba-minnesota-wild-five-year-deal |access-date=November 20, 2023}} On June 8, 2020, Dumba became an inaugural executive board member of the [[Hockey Diversity Alliance]], whose goal is to address intolerance and racism in hockey.{{cite press release |title=Hockey Diversity Alliance formed by seven current, former NHL players |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |date=June 8, 2020 |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/hockey-diversity-alliance-formed-current-former-nhl-players-317116848 |access-date=November 20, 2023}} Dumba was named the 2020 [[King Clancy Memorial Trophy|King Clancy Award]] winner by the NHL for his efforts supporting community initiatives in [[Minneapolis]] and as a member of the Hockey Diversity Alliance.{{cite web |title=Wild's Matt Dumba named winner of 2020 King Clancy Memorial Trophy |work=[[Sportsnet]] |date=September 6, 2020 |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/wilds-matt-dumba-named-winner-2020-king-clancy-memorial-trophy/ |access-date=November 20, 2023}} During the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]], Dumba scored four goals and 14 points in 79 games and was third in ice time among Wild defencemen.{{cite press release |title=Dumba signs 1-year contract with Coyotes |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |date=August 7, 2023 |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/matt-dumba-signs-deal-with-arizona-344850370 |access-date=November 20, 2023}} ====Arizona Coyotes==== After the Wild chose to not re-sign Dumba during the 2023 off-season, Dumba signed as an [[unrestricted free agent]] to a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the [[Arizona Coyotes]] on August 7, 2023. Dumba made his Arizona debut on October 13, 2023 versus the New Jersey Devils. He scored his first goal in a Coyotes' uniform on [[Akira Schmid]] to open the scoring in the 4–3 victory over the Devils.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401559253 |title=Bjugstad and Schmaltz score in shootout as Coyotes beat Devils 4–3 |work=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=October 13, 2023 |access-date=July 16, 2024}} He played in 58 games for Arizona, scoring four goals and ten points.{{cite press release |title=Lightning acquire D Matt Dumba and a 2025 seventh-round pick from Arizona |date=March 8, 2024 |publisher=[[Tampa Bay Lightning]] |via=NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/lightning-acquire-d-matt-dumba-and-a-seventh-round-pick-from-arizona |access-date=March 9, 2024}} ====Tampa Bay Lightning==== On March 8, 2024, the Coyotes traded Dumba along with a [[2025 NHL entry draft|2025]] seventh-round pick to the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in exchange for a [[2027 NHL entry draft|2027]] fifth-round pick. He made his Lightning debut on March 9 in a 7–0 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers.{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/lightning/2024/03/09/anthony-duclair-matt-dumba-flyers-victor-hedman-andrei-vasilevskiy/ |title=3 keys to Lightning's dominant shutout win over the Flyers |work=Tampa Bay Times |last=Encina |first=Eduardo A. |date=March 9, 2024 |access-date=July 16, 2024}} Dumba recorded his first point with the Lightning, an assist on [[Michael Eyssimont]]'s goal in the first period, in a 7–4 win over the Montreal Canadiens on April 4, 2024.{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-mtl/2024/04/04/2023021204 |title=Kucherov, Lightning defeat Canadiens, gain in Atlantic |publisher=National Hockey League |date=April 4, 2024 |access-date=July 16, 2024}} He played in 18 regular season games with Tampa Bay, registering two points.{{cite web |title=Stars sign Matt Dumba to a two-year contract |url= https://www.nhl.com/stars/news/dallas-stars-sign-defenseman-matt-dumba-to-a-two-year-contract-070124 |via=NHL.com |publisher=Dallas Stars |access-date=July 15, 2024 |date=July 1, 2024}} Dumba made his [[2024 Stanley Cup playoffs]] debut with the Lightning on April 21 in 3–2 loss to the Florida Panthers in the opening round.{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-fla/2024/04/21/2023030111/boxscore |title=Verhaeghe scores in 3rd period, Panthers edge Lightning in Game 1 |publisher=National Hockey League |date=April 21, 2024 |access-date=July 16, 2024}} He played in five playoff games with the Lightning, finishing second on the team in blocked shots with seven as the Lightning were eliminated from the postseason.{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/panthers-win-battle-of-florida-eliminate-lightning-in-five-games/ |title=Panthers win Battle of Florida, eliminate Lightning in five games |work=Sportsnet |agency=Associated Press |date=April 29, 2024 |access-date=July 16, 2024}} ====Dallas Stars==== On July 1, 2024, Dumba signed as an unrestricted free agent to a two-year, $7.5 million contract with the [[Dallas Stars]]. ====Pittsburgh Penguins and retirement==== One year into his tenure with Dallas, Dumba was traded to the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] on July 10, 2025, alongside a second-round draft pick in [[2028 NHL entry draft|2028]], in exchange for [[Vladislav Kolyachonok]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/matt-dumba-pick-traded-to-pittsburgh-by-dallas-for-vladislav-kolyachonok |title=Dumba, 2028 draft pick traded to Penguins by Stars |website=NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League |date=July 10, 2025}} On December 12, 2025, Dumba was waived by the Pittsburgh Penguins and after going unclaimed, reported to their AHL affiliate, the [[Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins]].{{Cite web |date=2025-12-12 |title=Penguins place defenseman Matt Dumba on waivers |url=https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/news/pittsburgh-penguins-place-defenseman-matt-dumba-waivers |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Daily Faceoff}}{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Sportsnet |date=2025-12-12 |title=Penguins place defenceman Matt Dumba on waivers |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/penguins-placing-defenceman-matt-dumba-on-waivers/ |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Sportsnet}} Prior to the [[2026 Calder Cup playoffs|2025–26 AHL playoffs]] on April 16, 2026, the Penguins placed Dumba on unconditional waivers for the purposes of terminating his contract.{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/article/penguins-d-dumba-placed-on-waivers-for-purpose-of-contract-termination/ |title=Penguins place D Dumba on unconditional waivers just ahead of playoffs |work=TSN |date=April 16, 2026 |access-date=April 20, 2026}} Dumba announced his retirement from professional hockey on October 9, 2026.{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/matt-dumba-retires-from-nhl-after-13-seasons |title=Dumba retires after 13 seasons in NHL |website=NHL.com |date=October 9, 2026 |access-date=October 11, 2026}} Floyd]], some [[NHL]] players formed the [[Hockey Diversity Alliance]], which Dumba joined. On August 1, 2020, Dumba became the first player to [[U.S. national anthem protests (2016–present)|kneel during the U.S. national anthem]]. Though he was a member of the [[Minnesota Wild]], he was not playing that night. Two Black players from the teams who were playing placed their hands on his shoulders while he knelt: [[Malcolm Subban]] of the [[Chicago Blackhawks]] and [[Darnell Nurse]] of the [[Edmonton Oilers]]. The three of them remained in this position during both the American and Canadian national anthems. born '''Lee Ho-dong''' ({{Korean|이호동}}) on {{birth date|1991|03|28}}{{cite book|author=Mark Russell|title=K-Pop Now!: The Korean Music Revolution|page=63|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=etDZAwAAQBAJ|date=April 29, 2014|publisher=Tuttle Publishing|isbn=978-1-4629-1411-1}}), known professionally as '''Hoya''', is a South Korean singer, rapper, songwriter, actor, and dancer, currently a member of the dance crew [[Be Mbitious|Mbitious]]. Hoya made his acting debut in the drama ''[[Reply 1997]]'' (2012) and went on to star in the dramas ''[[My Lovely Girl]]'' (2014), ''[[Mask (2015 TV series)|Mask]]'' (2015), ''[[Radiant Office]]'' (2017), and ''[[Two Cops (TV series)|Two Cops]]'' (2017), ''[[Devilish Charm]]'' (2018). ==Biography== Hoya was born in [[Busan]], South Korea. He dropped out of high school during his first year to pursue his dream as a singer. His father was against the decision thus Hoya had to leave home. He then took the high school qualification exam and passed. Later his father accepted him and now supports Infinite whole heartedly. Hoya auditioned after he dropped out and ended up in his current agency, [[Woollim Entertainment]]. He was a former [[JYP Entertainment]] trainee.{{cite web|title=호야 자퇴 심경고백, "교복 못 입은 아쉬움...'응답'으로 보상받아"|url=http://news.naver.com/main/read.nhn?mode=LSD&mid=sec&sid1=106&oid=038&aid=0002303233|publisher=[[Naver News]]|access-date=September 24, 2012}} On March 10, 2014, he announced that his real birth name is Lee Hodong, not Howon as he had previously told the public, and that he changed it in order not to share a name with comedian [[Kang Ho-dong|Kang Hodong]].{{cite web|title=Infinite's Hoya Changed His Name Because of Kang Ho Dong|url=http://www.mnetamerica.com/news/article/60635/infinite-hoya-talks-about-changing-his-name-from-leehodong|website=[[Mnet (TV channel)|Mnet]]|date=March 10, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126185452/http://www.mnetamerica.com/news/article/60635/infinite-hoya-talks-about-changing-his-name-from-leehodong|url-status=dead}} Hoya graduated from [[Daekyeung University]], majoring in Applied Music.{{cite web|title=인피니트 5명, 오늘 같은 대학 동시 졸업..수상도|url=http://m.news.naver.com/read.nhn?mode=LSD&sid1=001&oid=108&aid=0002200649}}{{cite web|title=5 Infinite Members to Graduate from University Together|url=http://english.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/CU/content/cms_view_1795763.jsp?cid=1795763&nodeId=4396|website=enewsWorld|date=February 15, 2013|access-date=September 11, 2018|archive-date=July 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180710102253/http://english.visitkorea.or.kr/enu/CU/content/cms_view_1795763.jsp?cid=1795763&nodeId=4396|url-status=dead}} [[File:Korea KPOP World Festival 46.jpg|thumb|upright=1|right|Hoya at [[K-Pop World Festival]] 2013.]] ==Career== ===2010: Debut with Infinite=== {{Main article|Infinite (band)}} Hoya debuted as rapper, vocal and main dancer of South Korean boyband [[Infinite (group)|Infinite]] in 2010. The group officially debuted on June 9, 2010. ===2012–2014: Infinite H's debut and acting roles=== {{Main article|Infinite H}} Hoya made his acting debut in the tvN drama ''[[Reply 1997]]''. The drama was a major hit and raised his popularity.{{cite web|title=[Interview] Hoya is More Popular Because of ′Reply 1997′ Than Infinite|url=http://mwave.interest.me/enewsworld/en/article/27393/hoya-says-people-dont-recognize-him-as-hoya-but-as-kang-jun-hee|work=enewsWorld|date=January 27, 2013|archive-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305023107/http://mwave.interest.me/enewsworld/en/article/27393/hoya-says-people-dont-recognize-him-as-hoya-but-as-kang-jun-hee|url-status=bot: unknown}} In September 2012, Hoya and fellow Infinite member [[Jang Dong-woo|Dongwoo]] formed a subgroup called [[Infinite H]].{{cite web|title=[INTERVIEW] INFINITE H – Part 1|url=http://en.tenasia.com/archives/58258|work=10Asia|date=June 3, 2013|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127083856/http://en.tenasia.com/archives/58258|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=[INTERVIEW] INFINITE H – Part 2|url=http://en.tenasia.com/archives/58361|work=10Asia|date=June 3, 2013|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126191147/http://en.tenasia.com/archives/58361|url-status=dead}} The subgroup released their first mini-album, titled ''[[Fly High (EP)|Fly High]],'' in January 2013.{{cite web|title=INFINITE H new album coming soon|url=http://kpopherald.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=201501201837299143665_2&ACE_SEARCH=1|work=[[Kpop Herald]]|date=January 20, 2015|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116192233/http://kpopherald.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=201501201837299143665_2&ACE_SEARCH=1|url-status=live}} In 2014, Hoya starred in SBS' music romance drama, ''[[My Lovely Girl]]''; which co-stars his fellow Infinite member [[Kim Myung-soo]].{{cite web|title=Infinite's L and Hoya Confirmed for Drama 'My Lovely Girl'|url=http://mwave.interest.me/en/kpop-news/article-print/72629/|work=enewsWorld|date=August 5, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126185356/http://mwave.interest.me/en/kpop-news/article-print/72629/|url-status=live}} On September 24, 2014, Hoya was cast as the lead role in the film ''[[Hiya (film)|Hiya]]''. {{Short description|American rapper (born 1993)}} {{Use American English|date=August 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2026}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Wiki | image = Wiki (rapper).jpg | caption = Morales performing in 2021 | birth_name = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1993|10|21}} | birth_place = [[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]], U.S. | genre = [[East Coast hip-hop]] | occupation = {{hlist|Rapper|songwriter|record producer}} | instrument = Vocals | years_active = 2011–present | label = {{hlist|Wikset|Letter Racer|[[XL Recordings|XL]]}} | past_member_of = {{hlist|[[Ratking (group)|Ratking]]|Secret Circle}} | website = {{url|wikset.nyc}} }} '''Patrick G. Morales''' (born October 21, 1993), better known by his [[stage name]] '''Wiki''', is an American rapper and record producer. He was a member of New York City-based [[hip-hop]] group [[Ratking (group)|Ratking]] with rapper-producer [[Sporting Life (musician)|Sporting Life]] and rapper [[Hak (musician)|Hak]], which disbanded in 2016.{{Cite web |last=Kamalakanthan |first=Prashanth |title=RATKING: Gritty, grimy, hip-hop that totally grows on you. |url=https://www.motherjones.com/media/2014/11/ratking-interview-wiki93-so-it-goes-sporting-life-hak/ |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=Mother Jones |language=en-US}} Morales was also a member of Secret Circle with rapper [[Antwon]] and rapper-producer [[Travis Miller (musician)|Lil Ugly Mane]] until 2018.{{Cite web |date=May 22, 2018 |title=Antwon, Wiki, And Lil Ugly Mane Release Statements After Secret Circle Break Up |url=https://stereogum.com/1997391/secret-circle-break-up/news/ |access-date=March 15, 2026 |website=stereogum.com |language=en}} He has since released four solo albums; ''[[No Mountains in Manhattan]]'' (2017), ''[[Oofie]]'' (2019), ''[[Half God]]'' (2021), and ''[[Ancient History (album)|Ancient History]]'' (2026). ==Biography== Wiki was raised on the [[Upper West Side]] in [[Manhattan]]. He attended the [[Brooklyn Friends School]], and is of Puerto Rican ancestry on his father's side and Irish-American on his mother's side. His mother grew up in suburban [[Westchester County, New York]]. He began his music career in 2011 as a member of the New York City hip-hop group [[Ratking (group)|Ratking]] with [[Hak (musician)|Hak]] and [[Sporting Life (musician)|Sporting Life]].Brian Josephs, [https://www.spin.com/2017/08/wiki-interview-no-mountains-in-manhattan/ "Interview: Wiki Talks New Album No Mountains in Manhattan and the Future of Ratking,"] ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]'', August 28, 2017. In a 2012 interview, he stated that his rap name is an allusion to [[Wikipedia]].Ahmed, Insanul. "[https://www.complex.com/music/2012/03/who-is-wiki/growing-up Who is Wiki?]" ''[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]''. March 28, 2012. Wiki released his debut solo extended play ''1993'' on October 2, 2011. ''1993'' was later re-released as Ratking's debut extended play ''Wiki93'' on November 2, 2012. Ratking released their debut single "100" on November 18, 2013. They released their debut studio album ''[[So It Goes (Ratking album)|So It Goes]]'' on April 7, 2014.Tas Tobey, [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/12/08/style/wiki-hip-hop-ratking.html?_r=0 "Wiki, Formerly of the Hip-Hop Collective Ratking, Strikes Out on His Own,"] ''[[New York Times]]'', December 8, 2017. Ratking released their second extended play ''[[700-Fill]]'' on March 4, 2015. Wiki released his debut solo mixtape ''[[Lil Me]]'' on December 7, 2015. The album features guest appearances from [[Skepta]], [[Mica Levi]], [[King Krule]], and many others. Wiki and fellow rapper [[Your Old Droog]] released their collaborative extended play ''What Happened to Fire?'' on February 2, 2017. Wiki's debut solo album ''[[No Mountains in Manhattan]]'' was released months later on August 25, 2017. The album is named after a line from the 1973 [[Martin Scorsese]] film ''[[Mean Streets]]''. On November 8, 2019, Wiki released his second solo album, ''[[Oofie]]'', which includes features from [[Lil Ugly Mane]], [[Denzel Curry]], [[Princess Nokia]], and more.{{cite web |title=Wiki: OOFIE Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/wiki-oofie/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=May 5, 2026}} On May 7, 2021, Wiki released a collaborative album with producer NAH titled ''Telephonebooth.''{{cite web |title=Wiki / NAH: Telephonebooth Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/wiki-nah-telephonebooth/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=May 5, 2026}} Months later on October 1, 2021, he released the collaborative album ''[[Half God]]'' with producer [[Sage Elsesser|Navy Blue]].{{cite web |title=Wiki: Half God Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/wiki-half-god/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=May 5, 2026}} On September 22, 2023, Wiki released a collaborative album, ''[[Faith Is a Rock]]'', with rapper [[Mike (musician)|MIKE]] and producer [[The Alchemist (musician)|the Alchemist]].{{cite web |title=MIKE / Wiki / The Alchemist: Faith Is a Rock Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/mike-wiki-the-alchemist-faith-is-a-rock/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=May 5, 2026}} Wiki released a second collaborative album in 2023, titled ''14K Figaro.'' The album is fully produced by Tony Seltzer, featuring guest appearances from [[Zelooperz]] and [[Remy Banks]], among others.{{cite web |title=Wiki and Tony Seltzer Announce Album, Share New Song: Listen |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/wiki-and-tony-seltzer-announce-album-share-new-song-listen/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=May 5, 2026}} Wiki made a [[cameo appearance]] in the 2025 film ''[[Marty Supreme]]'', directed by [[Josh Safdie]].{{cite web |title=Ping-Pong Champions, Basketball Greats, Republican Power Brokers: Every Cameo in ‘Marty Supreme’ |url=https://typesetbrooklyn.com/articles/marty-supreme-cameos-list |publisher=Type.Set.Brooklyn |access-date=May 5, 2026}} On June 12, 2026, Wiki released his third solo album, ''[[Ancient History (album)|Ancient History]],'' with features from [[Duendita]], [[Your Old Droog]] and Salimata, as well as credited production from [[The Alchemist (musician)|The Alchemist]], [[Lil Ugly Mane]], [[Sage Elsesser|Navy Blue]] and [[Mike (musician)|DJ BlackPower]].{{cite web |title=Wiki: Ancient History Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/wiki-ancient-history/ |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=1 August 2026}} == Discography == {{See also|Ratking (group)#Discography}} === Studio albums === {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;" |+ List of studio albums, with year released ! '''Kadidiatou Diani''' (born 1 April 1995) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Women's Super League]] club [[London City Lionesses]] and the [[France women's national football team|France national team]].

==Club career==

===OL Lyonnes===
On 2 August 2023, Diani was announced at [[Olympique Lyonnais Féminin|Lyon]] on a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr/actualites/kadidiatou-diani-rejoint-l-olympique-lyonnais-pour-quatre-saisons|title=Kadidiatou Diani rejoint l'Olympique Lyonnais pour quatre saisons|trans-title=Kadidiatou Diani joins Olympique Lyonnais for four seasons|language=French|website=www.ol.fr}}</ref> A month later, on 27 September, an investigation was opened against her former coach [[Didier Ollé-Nicolle]], with Diani accusing him of sexual assault.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/sports/foot/psg/football-kadidiatou-diani-porte-plainte-pour-agression-sexuelle-contre-son-ancien-entraineur-au-psg_6088014.html|title=Football : Kadidiatou Diani porte plainte pour agression sexuelle contre son ancien entraîneur au PSG, une enquête ouverte|trans-title=Football: Kadidiatou Diani files sexual assault complaint against her former PSG coach, investigation opened|language=French|website=www.francetvinfo.fr |date=27 September 2023 }}</ref>

===London City Lionesses===
On 15 July 2026, Diani joined [[Women's Super League]] club [[London City Lionesses]] on a three-year deal, the Lionesses are the first fully independent team to be promoted to the top women's league.<ref name="guardian2019">{{cite web |last1=Wrack |first1=Suzanne |title='Equality has to be more than words': London City Lionesses go it alone |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/18/london-city-lionesses-millwall-womens-football |website=The Guardian |date=18 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Birmingham City 2-2 London City Lionesses: WSL promotion for independent club |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c15v1v9v1v0t |access-date=2025-05-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Both London City Lionesses and her former club Lyon are owned by businesswoman [[Michele Kang|Michelle Kang]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 July 2026 |title=Kadidiatou Diani joins London City Lionesses |url=https://www.londoncitylionesses.com/post/kadidiatou-diani-joins-london-city-lionesses |access-date=15 July 2026 |website=London City Lionesses |language=en}}</ref> The transfer fee was reported to be £500,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanders |first=Emma |date=14 July 2026 |title=Kadidiatou Diani: London City Lionesses sign France forward for more than £500,000 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvgjg66gyjxo |access-date=15 July 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== International career ==
Diani has played for [[France women's national football team|France]] at several youth levels, including in the [[2012 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup]], where she scored four goals and helped her side winning the championship.<ref name="fifa.com">{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=358573/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518105428/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=358573/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 May 2015 |title=FIFA Tournaments – Players & Coaches – Kadidiatou DIANI }}</ref> She also played in the [[2014 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]], scoring one goal against [[New Zealand women's national under-20 football team|New Zealand]] and helping France to finish in the third place.<ref name="fifa.com"/>

Diani was called up to the France squad for the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2017]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fff.fr/articles/equipes-de-france-1/details-articles/176226-les-joueuses-pour-l-euro|title=Les joueuses pour l'Euro 2017|date=30 May 2017|work=fff.fr|access-date=18 March 2025|archive-date=3 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201103082359/https://www.fff.fr/articles/equipes-de-france-1/details-articles/176226-les-joueuses-pour-l-euro|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Diani was called up to the France squad for the [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/equipe-de-france/actualites/l-equipe-de-france-sans-katoto-pour-la-coupe-du-monde-955806 |title=L'équipe de France sans Katoto pour la Coupe du monde|trans-title=The French team without Katoto for the World Cup |first=Cédric |last=Callier |newspaper=[[Le Figaro]] |date=2 May 2019}}</ref>

On 30 May 2022, Diani was called up to the France squad for the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2022]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Championnat d'Europe de l'UEFA 2022: Liste des joueuses retenues |url=https://media.fff.fr/uploads/files/2782fdcffc88597d793d4453e6b7afe4.pdf |website=Fédération Française de Football |date=30 May 2022}}</ref>

On 24 February 2023, she announced she would no longer play for the national team after captain [[Wendie Renard]] said she would step down to save her mental health. Diani said she wanted changes to be made to the way the team was managed.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-02-24 |title=France captain Renard to skip World Cup to 'preserve mental health', Diani, Katoto step down |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/france-captain-renard-will-not-play-world-cup-preserve-mental-health-2023-02-24/ |access-date=2023-02-24 |archive-date=24 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230224204551/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/france-captain-renard-will-not-play-world-cup-preserve-mental-health-2023-02-24/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Diani was called up to the France squad for the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Les vingt-trois Bleues retenues pour la Coupe du monde|trans-title=The twenty-three Blues selected for the World Cup|language=fr|url=https://www.fff.fr/article/10577-les-vingt-trois-bleues-retenues-pour-la-coupe-du-monde.html|publisher=[[French Football Federation]]|date=4 July 2023|archive-date=4 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704125347/https://www.fff.fr/article/10577-les-vingt-trois-bleues-retenues-pour-la-coupe-du-monde.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 August 2023, she scored a hat-trick in a 6–3 victory over [[Panama women's national football team|Panama]] in the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]] last group stage match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66380377 |title=Panama 3–6 France |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 August 2023 |access-date=2 August 2023 |archive-date=2 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230802232306/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66380377 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In July 2024, Diani was named in France's squad for the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2024 Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=JO 2024 : la liste définitive des Bleues d'Hervé Renard|url=https://www.footmercato.net/a3755298134096492710-jo-2024-la-liste-definitive-des-bleues-dherve-renard|language=fr|date=8 July 2024|access-date=9 July 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Diani was born in [[Ivry-sur-Seine]], France on 1 April 1995, and is of Malian descent.<ref>{{cite web|title=MONDIAL FÉMININ: KADIDIATOU DIANI, LA VITESSE AU SERVICE DES BLEUES|url=http://bamada.net/mondial-feminin-kadidiatou-diani-la-vitesse-au-service-des-bleues|date=28 May 2019|access-date=23 December 2022|archive-date=23 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221223071844/http://bamada.net/mondial-feminin-kadidiatou-diani-la-vitesse-au-service-des-bleues|url-status=live}}</ref>

Her "adviser", César Mavacala, was a suspect in the [[Hamraoui case]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harpur |first=Charlotte |title=Kheira Hamraoui suffered an attack of 'violent jealousy'. Two years on, this story is far from over |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5019984/2023/11/04/psg-kheira-hamraoui-was-beaten-with-an-iron-bar-two-years-on-this-story-is-far-from-over/ |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=The Athletic |date=8 November 2023 |language=en |archive-date=10 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110214346/https://theathletic.com/5019984/2023/11/04/psg-kheira-hamraoui-was-beaten-with-an-iron-bar-two-years-on-this-story-is-far-from-over/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2022, she caused a controversy with [[Marie-Antoinette Katoto]] for her support to [[Aminata Diallo]] during a goal celebration for [[France women's national football team|France]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 22, 2022 |title=Equipe de France: la célébration "Aminata Diallo" de Katoto et Diani. |url=https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/equipe-de-france/equipe-de-france-la-celebration-aminata-diallo-de-katoto-et-diani-contre-les-pays-bas_AV-202202220611.html |website=RMC Sports |language=French}}</ref>

'''Giorgia Whigham''' (born August 18, 1997<ref>{{Cite Instagram |author=Giorgia Whigham |user=giorgia_whigham |postid=CwGO9xvJ5Ld |date=August 18, 2023 |title=Weird post but I turn 26 today and am doing a lot of reflecting |access-date=July 20, 2024}}</ref>) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as Kat in the first season of ''[[13 Reasons Why]]'', [[Amy Bendix]] in the [[The Punisher season 2|second season]] of ''[[The Punisher (TV series)|The Punisher]]'', Beth in the third season of ''[[Scream (TV series)|Scream]]'', Lysella in ''[[The Orville]]'' and Blaire in ''[[Ted (TV series)|Ted]]''.

==Life and career==
Giorgia Whigham is the daughter of actor [[Shea Whigham]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Surrey |first1=Miles |title='Punisher' Season 2 Is a Relic of Marvel's Failures on Netflix |url=https://www.theringer.com/tv/2019/1/23/18193296/punisher-season-2-netflix-marvel-flaws |publisher=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] |accessdate=January 24, 2020 |language=en |date=23 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250408232253/https://www.theringer.com/2019/01/23/tv/punisher-season-2-netflix-marvel-flaws |url-status= live|archive-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref> She had her first break in the acting world starring alongside [[Ellery Sprayberry]] in the 2016 short film ''Pinky''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2017/09/173069/giorgia-whigham-actress-pinky|title=Giorgia Whigham On Her Role In Pinky, Bullying & Mean Girls|date=September 22, 2017|first=Jessica|last=Chou|work=Refinery29|access-date=December 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612163210/https://www.refinery29.com/amp/2017/09/173069/giorgia-whigham-actress-pinky|archive-date=June 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Following her acting debut, she won roles on a variety of TV shows including ''[[Shameless (American TV series)|Shameless]]'', ''[[Son of Zorn]]'', ''[[13 Reasons Why]]'', and ''[[The Orville]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dintelman |first=Nicole |date=April 10, 2017 |title=13 Reasons Why: Tape 1, Side A |url=http://starrymag.com/13-reasons-why-tape-1-side-a/ |work=Starry Constellation Magazine}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/in-a-weak-episode-the-orville-tackles-social-media-for-1819901374|title=In a weak episode, The Orville tackles social media for no good reason|work=AV Club|first=Nick|last=Wanserski|date=October 27, 2017 }}</ref> On September 13, 2017, it was announced that Whigham would join the third season of the [[VH1]] slasher television series ''[[Scream (TV series)|Scream]]'' as a series regular. She starred in the role of Beth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/09/scream-keke-palmer-rj-cyler-jessica-sula-giorgia-whigham-giullian-yao-gioiello-season-3-cast-1202169106/|title='Scream': Keke Palmer, RJ Cyler, Jessica Sula, More Round Out Season 3 Cast|last = Petski|first = Denise|date = September 13, 2017|work = Deadline|access-date = September 13, 2017}}</ref> The third season premiered on July 8, 2019.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://etcanada.com/news/467876/scream-reboot-gets-trailer-with-cameo-from-paris-jackson/|title='Scream' Reboot Gets Trailer With Cameo From Paris Jackson|last=Samhan|first=Jamie|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|date=June 24, 2019|access-date=June 25, 2019|archive-date=June 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626202446/https://etcanada.com/news/467876/scream-reboot-gets-trailer-with-cameo-from-paris-jackson/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 26, 2018, it was announced that Whigham would appear in the second season of [[Netflix]]'s ''[[The Punisher (TV series)|The Punisher]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2018/02/marvels-the-punisher-josh-stewart-floriana-lima-giorgia-whigham-season-2-cast-netflix-series-1202301689/|title='Marvel's The Punisher': Josh Stewart, Floriana Lima & Giorgia Whigham Join Cast Of Netflix Series For Season 2|last1 = Andreeva|first1 = Nellie|last2= Petski|first2=Denise|date = February 26, 2018|work = Deadline|access-date = February 26, 2018}}</ref> In 2019, she co-starred in the film ''[[Saving Zoë (2019 film)|Saving Zoë]]'', which was an adaptation to [[Alyson Noël]]’s bestselling young adult novel of the same title, starring alongside sisters [[Laura Marano]] and [[Vanessa Marano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/08/studio71-saving-zoe-laura-vanessa-marano-urbanworld-film-festival-2017-lineup-film-briefs-1202154853/|title=Studio71 Aboard 'Saving Zoë' Film With Laura & Vanessa Marano; Urbanworld Film Festival Unveils Lineup — Film Briefs|last = N'Duka|first = Amanda|date = August 23, 2017|work = Deadline|access-date = December 11, 2017}}</ref> In 2017 and 2022, she guest-starred as Lysella on the first and third seasons of ''[[The Orville]]''. In 2022, she was cast as Blaire Bennett on the Peacock series ''[[Ted (TV series)|Ted]]'', the television prequel of [[Ted (film)|the film of the same name]].<ref name="cast_Deadline">{{cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |title=''Ted'': Giorgia Whigham, Max Burkholder & Scott Grimes Join Seth MacFarlane In Peacock Series Based On Films |url=https://deadline.com/2022/04/giorgia-whigham-max-burkholder-scott-grimes-cast-ted-seth-macfarlane-peacock-series-1235001608/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=13 April 2022 |date=April 13, 2022}}</ref>

'''Nicolás Iván González''' ({{IPA|es|nikoˈlas iˈβaŋ ɡonˈsales}}; born 6 April 1998) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and the [[Argentina national football team|Argentina national team]].

==Club career==
===Argentinos Juniors===
After over ten years in the club's youth system,<ref name="Argentinos profile">{{Cite news|title=Nicolás González profile|url=http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/profesional/plantel/perfil/2522_nicolasgonzalez|website=Argentinos Juniors|date=2 November 2017|language=es|archive-date=9 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109052833/http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/profesional/plantel/perfil/2522_nicolasgonzalez |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Argentinos interview">{{Cite news|title=Conociendo a Nicolás González|url=http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/amateur/juvenil/noticias/20160525_5826|website=Argentinos Juniors|access-date=2 November 2017|language=es|archive-date=7 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107030208/http://www.argentinosjuniors.com.ar/futbol/amateur/juvenil/noticias/20160525_5826 |url-status=dead }}</ref> González made his professional debut for [[Argentinos Juniors]] in a [[2015–16 Copa Argentina]] defeat to [[Deportivo Laferrere]] of [[Primera C Metropolitana]] in July 2016.<ref name="Soccerway profile">{{Cite news|date=2 November 2017|title=Nicolás González profile|work=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/nicolas-gonzalez/450709/|access-date=2 November 2017}}</ref> He made his [[Primera B Nacional]] debut on 28 August against [[San Martín de Tucumán|San Martín]] prior to scoring the first of his four goals in [[2016–17 Primera B Nacional|2016–17]] on 23 April 2017, getting the winner against [[Club Atlético Paraná|Atlético Paraná]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> In total, González made twenty appearances in 2016–17, a season which ended with Argentinos winning promotion to the [[Argentine Primera División]].<ref name="Soccerway profile" /><ref name="BDFA profile">{{Cite news|title=Nicolás González profile|url=http://www.bdfa.com.ar/jugadores-NICOLAS-GONZALEZ-108541.html|website=Argentine Primera División|date=2 November 2017|language=es}}</ref><ref name="Argentinos promotion">{{Cite news|title=¡Gritalo Bicho!: González y el gol del ascenso|url=http://www.tycsports.com/futbol/gritalo-bicho-gonzalez-y-el-gol-del-ascenso|website=[[TyC Sports]]|date=8 July 2017|access-date=2 November 2017|language=es}}</ref> He scored on his first top-flight start, scoring the opening goal in a defeat to [[Club Atlético Belgrano|Belgrano]].<ref name="Soccerway profile"/>

===VfB Stuttgart===
[[File:NicolasGonzalez (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|279x279px|González with [[VfB Stuttgart]] in 2019]]
On 10 July 2018, González signed a five-year contract with [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref name="VfB Stuttgart 1">{{Cite news|title=VfB sign Nicolás Gonzalez|url=http://www.vfb.de/en/vfb/latest/news/professionals/2018/vfb-stuttgart-verpflichtet-nicolas-gonzalez-/|website=VfB Stuttgart|date=10 July 2018|access-date=10 July 2018}}</ref> He scored twice on his unofficial debut for the club, netting in a friendly victory over [[FV Illertissen]] on 18 July.<ref name="VfB Stuttgart 2">{{Cite news|title=FV Illertissen vs. VfB Stuttgart|url=https://www.vfb.de/en/vfb/latest/news/friendly-match/2018/fv-illertissen-vfb-stuttgart-/|date=18 July 2018|access-date=27 July 2018}}</ref> His first competitive goal arrived during a home loss to [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] on 22 December.<ref name="Soccerway profile" /> They were relegated at the end of [[2018–19 VfB Stuttgart season|2018–19]], with González subsequently scoring the winner on his [[2. Bundesliga]] bow against [[FC St. Pauli]] on 17 August 2019.<ref name="STN1">{{Cite news|title=Überglücklicher Nicolas Gonzalez|url=https://www.stuttgarter-nachrichten.de/inhalt.siegtorschuetze-des-vfb-stuttgart-uebergluecklicher-nicolas-gonzalez.438152be-b869-4fa6-a422-daca1326ed55.html|website=Stuttgarter Nachrichten|date=17 August 2019}}</ref> He scored consecutive braces in June 2020 against [[SV Sandhausen|Sandhausen]] and [[1. FC Nürnberg|Nürnberg]], the latter of which was his 100th league appearance for Stuttgart.<ref name="Soccerway profile" /><ref name="MA1">{{Cite news|title=Nicolas Gonzalez scores twice for Stuttgart as Bundesliga promotion nears|url=https://mundoalbiceleste.com/2020/06/22/nicolas-gonzalez-scores-twice-for-stuttgart-as-bundesliga-promotion-nears/|website=Mundo Albiceleste|date=22 June 2020|access-date=26 June 2020}}</ref>

On 25 November 2020, González extended his contract with VfB Stuttgart until June 2024.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nicolas Gonzalez signs contract extension|url=https://www.vfb.de/en/vfb/latest/news/professionals/2020/vertragsverlaengerung-nicolas-gonzalez/|website=VfB Stuttgart|date=25 November 2020}}</ref>

===Fiorentina===
On 23 June 2021, González signed a five-year contract with [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] until 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Welcome, Nicolás González!|url=http://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2021-06-23/welcome-nicolas-gonzalez|website=ACF Fiorentina|date=23 June 2021|access-date=23 June 2021|archive-date=29 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629014331/https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2021-06-23/welcome-nicolas-gonzalez|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 13 August, González made his debut for Fiorentina in a 4–0 win against [[Serie B]] side [[Cosenza Calcio|Cosenza]] in the first round of [[Coppa Italia]] scoring the second goal in the 37th minute.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Buona la prima per Italiano: poker della Fiorentina al Cosenza. Sugli scudi Vlahovic e Nico Gonzalez|url=https://www.fiorentinanews.com/buona-la-prima-per-italiano-poker-della-fiorentina-al-cosenza-sugli-scudi-vlahovic-e-nico-gonzalez/|website=Fiorentina News|date=13 August 2021|language=it}}</ref> On 18 May 2023, González scored a brace in Fiorentina's second leg [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] semi-final victory against [[FC Basel|Basel]], sending his side to the [[2023 UEFA Europa Conference League final|final]] against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].{{Citation needed|date=April 2024}}

=== Juventus ===
On 25 August 2024, González joined [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nico Gonzalez is Bianconero! |url=https://www.juventus.com/en/news/articles/nico-gonzalez-is-bianconero |publisher=Juventus FC |access-date=25 August 2024 |date=25 August 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Gonzalez ceduto alla Juventus |url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/it/news/tutte/prima-squadra-maschile/2024-08-25/gonzalez-ceduto-alla-juventus |publisher=ACF Fiorentina |access-date=25 August 2024 |language=Italian |date=25 August 2024 }}</ref> Juventus reported the transfer fees as €8 million for the 2024–25 season loan (with up to €0.4 million in additional costs), followed by the permanent transfer for €25 million, with an additional performance-based fees up to €5 million. The obligation to buy is conditional, but the conditions are highly likely to be triggered, thus Juventus accounted for the move as a permanent transfer.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Juventus FC|url=https://www.juventus.com/images/image/private/fl_attachment/dev/lojkbuhysaztywvraj2l.pdf|title=AGREEMENT WITH FIORENTINA FOR THE ACQUISITION OF THE PLAYER DI GONZALEZ|date=25 August 2024}}</ref>

A month later, on 17 September, he scored his first goal on his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut in a 3–1 win over [[PSV Eindhoven]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Coates |first=Charlotte |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgwe4ke8d4t |title=Juventus 3–1 PSV |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 September 2024 }}</ref> In summer 2025, Juventus signed González permanently for a reported transfer fee of €28.1 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://oldjuve.com/juventus-open-to-offers-for-winger-they-only-just-bought |title=Juventus open to offers for winger they only just bought |publisher=oldjuve.com |date=17 July 2025 }}</ref>

==== Loan to Atlético Madrid ====
On 1 September 2025, González joined [[La Liga]] club [[Atlético Madrid]] on an initial loan deal worth €1 million with an obligation to buy for €35 million depending on the number of games he  plays for Atlético.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-01 |title=Club Atlético de Madrid - ¡Bienvenido, Nico Gonzalez! |url=https://www.atleticodemadrid.com/noticias/bienvenido-nico-gonzalez |access-date=2025-09-01 |website=Club Atlético de Madrid |language=es-ES}}</ref> He made his debut on 13 September in a league match against Villarreal CF, scoring a goal to help seal a 2–0 victory in his first appearance for the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-13 |title=Nicolás González scores on debut for Atlético Madrid in 2-0 win vs. Villarreal {{!}} Mundo Albiceleste |url=https://mundoalbiceleste.com/2025/09/13/nicolas-gonzalez-scores-on-debut-for-atletico-madrid-in-2-0-win-vs-villarreal/ |access-date=2025-09-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Nicolas Gonzalez Argentina v Egypt 7 July 2026-026.jpg|thumb|upright|González during the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]]]

In July 2019, González received a call-up from the [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina Olympic Team]] for said year's [[Football at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|Pan American Games]] in Peru.<ref name="AFA1">{{Cite news|title=Lista de convocados de la Selección Sub 23 para los Juegos Panamericanos|url=https://www.afa.com.ar/es/posts/lista-de-convocados-de-la-seleccion-sub-23-para-los-juegos-panamericanos|date=17 July 2019|access-date=29 July 2019|language=es}}</ref> After receiving a red card on his debut against [[Ecuador national under-20 football team|Ecuador]],<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nico González y su debut: "Lo disfruté al máximo"|trans-title=Nico González and his debut: "I enjoyed it to the fullest"|url=https://argentina.as.com/argentina/2019/10/13/futbol/1570992768_891716.html|website=[[Diario AS]]|date=13 October 2019|language=es}}</ref> he played again in the semi-final and the gold medal match when Argentina won the tournament.<ref name="Soccerway profile"/> Months later, González was selected by [[Lionel Scaloni]]'s [[Argentina national football team|senior team]] for the first time ahead of October friendly matches against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]].<ref name="AFA2">{{Cite news|title=Lista de convocados de la Selección Mayor y Sub 23 para la doble fecha FIFA de octubre|url=https://www.afa.com.ar/es/posts/lista-de-convocados-de-la-seleccion-mayor-y-sub-23-para-la-doble-fecha-fifa-de-octubre|website=Argentine Football Association|date=27 September 2019|access-date=13 October 2019|language=es}}</ref><ref name="CLA1">{{Cite news|title=Quién es Nicolás González, el juvenil que juega en la B de Alemania y fue titular en la Selección |work=Clarín |url=https://www.clarin.com/deportes/nicolas-gonzalez-argentina-ecuador_0_s0bLfOQD.html|date=12 October 2019|access-date=13 October 2019|language=es}}</ref> He did not feature in the matchday squad against Germany, but appeared for his international bow during a 6–1 victory over Ecuador at the [[Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero]] in [[Elche]] on 13 October.<ref name="Soccerway profile"/>

González scored his first goal for Argentina on 12 November 2020 in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2022 FIFA World Cup]] qualifier against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] that ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref name="Soccerway profile"/>{{Better source needed|reason=Source does not clarify if it is his first goal|date=April 2024}} He netted again days later against the same opponent.{{Citation needed|date=April 2024}}

González was a member of the [[2021 Copa América]] winning side, making five appearances in the tournament, four as a starter and one as substitute in the [[2021 Copa América Final|final]] against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]]. He was also called up to Argentina's [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] squad, but was forced to withdraw with a muscular injury three days before the start of the tournament, being replaced by [[Ángel Correa]].<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=Argentina|number=1593315253227487233|title=#SelecciónMayor Tras el entrenamiento de hoy, el futbolista Nicolás González sufrió una lesión muscular y quedará desafectado de la nómina mundialista. En su reemplazo, el CT de @Argentina, convoca a Ángel Correa.|date=17 November 2022}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=April 2024}}

In June 2024, González was included in Lionel Scaloni's final 26-man Argentina squad for the [[2024 Copa América]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 June 2024 |title=Lionel Scaloni dio a conocer la lista de la Selección argentina para la Copa América 2024 |url=https://tn.com.ar/deportes/futbol/2024/06/15/lionel-scaloni-dio-a-conocer-la-lista-de-la-seleccion-argentina-para-la-copa-america-2024/?gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAjwqf20BhBwEiwAt7dtdeK13_I24H4iqEBua7UtmDLn6_x-FfDm-gzEseLS8vJCnOlmjC3PlBoCHEwQAvD_BwE |access-date=23 July 2024 |work=Todo Noticias}}</ref> During the final against [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]], González had to replace [[Lionel Messi]] after he suffered an ankle injury in the second half. 18 minutes after he entered the pitch he scored a goal, but it was ruled off.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Cristofanelli |first=Federico |date=15 July 2024 |title=El boletín de calificaciones de Argentina en la final ante Colombia: los puntos superlativos que maquillaron la baja de Messi y Lautaro Martínez héroe |url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2024/07/15/el-boletin-de-calificaciones-de-argentina-en-la-final-ante-colombia-los-puntos-superlativos-que-maquillaron-la-baja-de-messi-y-lautaro-martinez-heroe/ |access-date=23 July 2024 |website=Infobae}}</ref>

On 27 May 2026, González  was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/argentina-squad-announced|title=Messi headlines star-studded Argentina squad|date=27 May 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref> During the tournament, he was primarily used as a substitute, making several impactful appearances off the bench as Argentina progressed to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nicolás González: Argentina's FIFA World Cup super sub, made in the Bundesliga |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/nicolas-gonzalez-argentina-fifa-world-cup-super-sub-stuttgart-38267 |publisher=[[Bundesliga]] |date=16 July 2026}}</ref> In the final against [[Spain national football team|Spain]], he became the fifth player to make his first-ever FIFA World Cup start in a final, after [[Gyula Polgár]], [[Jiří Tichý]], [[Gustavo Dezotti]] and [[Christoph Kramer]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carr |first=Harry |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/spain-vs-argentina-stats-2026-world-cup-final |title=Spain 1-0 Argentina Stats (aet): Torres Decides World Cup Final as Fernández Sees Red and Messi Falls Short |publisher=Opta Analyst |date=19 July 2026 }}</ref>

'''Martín Daniel Ezcurra''' (born April 23, 1987) is an [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[palaeontologist]] who has assisted in the naming of several extinct [[genera]] such as ''[[Aerotitan]]'', ''[[Lophostropheus]]'' and ''[[Powellvenator]]''.

==Biography==
Ezcurra was born on April 23, 1987. He first got into [[paleontology]] in 2002 while working with [[Fernando Novas]] in Argentina. He went to university in Buenos Aires, Munich, and Birmingham. His first papers were published in 2006.<ref>Novas F.E., Ezcurra M.D., and Agnolin F.L. 2006. Humerus of a basal abelisauroid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia. Revista del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales 8: 63-68.</ref><ref>Ezcurra M.D. 2006. A review of the systematic position of the dinosauriform archosaur ''[[Eucoelophysis baldwini]]'' from the Upper Triassic of New Mexico, USA. Geodiversitas 28: 649-684.</ref> Martin Ezcurra obtained his Master's-level<ref>2012 – Licenciado (= Master’s degree), Universidad de Buenos Aires (Argentina)</ref> studies in 2012 at the [[Universidad de Buenos Aires]] ([[Argentina]]) with specialization in animal anatomy and systematics. As an undergraduate student, Martin conducted since 2002 research on basal [[dinosaurs]] and [[theropods]] under the advice of [[Fernando Novas]] in the [[Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales]] ([[Buenos Aires, Argentina]]). In 2012, Martin moved to [[LMU Munich]] ([[Germany]]) and started his [[PhD]] research on basal archosauriforms under the advice of Richard Butler. In September 2013, Martin transferred to the [[University of Birmingham]] to continue his PhD research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ver Autor MARTIN DANIEL EZCURRA |url=https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/author/29347 |access-date=2024-08-06 |website=ri.conicet.gov.ar}}</ref>

On 30 September 2018, Breayley-Nati scored three tries in the Broncos' 34–12 [[2018 NRL Grand Final|Grand Final]] win over the [[Sydney Roosters Women|Sydney Roosters]]. She was awarded the inaugural Karyn Murphy Medal for Player of the Match.{{Cite web|url=https://www.broncos.com.au/news/2018/10/01/kimiora-nati-creates-her-own-piece-of-grand-final-history/|title=Kimiora Nati Creates Her Own Piece Of Grand Final History|date=30 September 2018|website=Brisbane Broncos}} On 13 October 2018, she started at {{rlp|hb}} in New Zealand's 24–26 loss to Australia.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrl.com/news/2018/10/01/kimiora-nati-heads-seven-brisbane-broncos-in-kiwi-ferns-squad/|title=Nati heads seven Broncos in Kiwi Ferns squad|date=1 October 2018|website=NRL}} During the loss, she ruptured her anterior cruciate ligament and tore he meniscus.{{Cite web|url=https://thewomensgame.com/news/nati-to-undergo-surgery-515579|title=Nati to undergo surgery|date=14 November 2018|website=The Women's Game}} On 26 June 2019, she joined the [[St. George Illawarra Dragons Women|St George Illawarra Dragons]] NRLW team.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dragons.com.au/news/2019/06/26/dragons-make-womens-premiership-statement-with-latest-signings/|title=Dragons make four significant Women's Premiership signings|date=26 June 2019|website=St George Illawarra Dragons}} In July 2019, she represented the [[Cook Islands women's national rugby league team|Cook Islands]] at the [[Rugby league nines at the 2019 Pacific Games|2019 Pacific Games]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.dragons.com.au/news/2019/07/09/new-dragons-make-pacific-womens-rl-history/|title=New Dragons make Pacific Women's RL history|date=9 July 2019|website=St George Illawarra Dragons}} In Round 1 of the [[2019 NRL Women's season]], she made her debut for the Dragons in a 4–14 loss to the [[Brisbane Broncos]]. She played just one game for the Dragons, missing the rest of the season due to a heart condition.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrl.com/news/2020/11/05/after-year-of-upheaval-breayley-eager-for-origin-return/|title=After year of upheaval, Breayley eager for Origin return|date=6 November 2020|website=NRL}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.nrl.com/players/womens-internationals/ferns/kimiora-nati/ NRL profile]{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} {{Brisbane Broncos squad - 2018 NRLW premiers}} {{New Zealand 2017 Women's Rugby League World Cup Squad}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Breayley-Nati, Kimiora}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century New Zealand sportswomen]] [[Category:Brisbane Broncos (NRLW) players]] [[Category:Cook Islands women's national rugby league team players]] [[Category:Gold Coast Titans (NRLW) players]] [[Category:New Zealand female rugby league players]] [[Category:New Zealand sportspeople of Cook Island descent]] [[Category:New Zealand women's national rugby league team players]] [[Category:Rugby league players from Auckland]] [[Category:St. George Illawarra Dragons (NRLW) players]] {{CookIslands-rugbyleague-bio-stub}} {{NewZealand-rugbyleague-bio-stub}}

'''Daniel da Silva dos Anjos''' (born 21 January 1996) is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[V.League 2]] club [[Becamex Ho Chi Minh City FC|Becamex Ho Chi Minh City]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Boa Esperança, Espírito Santo|Boa Esperança]], Anjos arrived at the youth academy of [[Figueirense Futebol Clube|Figueirense]] in 2012. On 12 April 2015, he made his first team debut in a 3–1 defeat against [[Joinville Esporte Clube|Joinville]] in the final of the [[Campeonato Catarinense]]. After being promoted to the first team in early 2016, he joined [[Flamengo]] on 30 March and was assigned to the under-20 team.<ref name="Anjos">{{cite web|title=Fla assina com Daniel dos Anjos, atacante de 20 anos, ex-Figueirense [Fla signs with Daniel dos Anjos, striker of 20 years, former Figueirense]|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/rj/futebol/noticia/2016/03/flamengo-assina-com-atacante-de-20-anos-ex-figueirense.amp|publisher=Globo Esporte|accessdate=26 December 2017|language=Portuguese|date=30 March 2016}}</ref> On 25 January 2017, he was loaned to the first team of [[Atlético Goianiense]] for the season's [[Campeonato Goiano]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dragão apresenta mais três: Daniel dos Anjos, Bruno Pacheco e Alípio [Dragon presents three more: Daniel dos Anjos, Bruno Pacheco and Alípio]|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/go/futebol/times/atletico-go/noticia/2017/01/dragao-apresenta-mais-tres-daniel-dos-anjos-alipio-e-bruno-pacheco.amp|publisher=Globo Esporte|accessdate=26 December 2017|language=Portuguese|date=25 January 2017}}</ref>

After being released by the ''Mengão'' in July 2017,<ref>{{cite web|title=Atacante do Flamengo é liberado e está próximo de assinar com o Benfica [Flamengo striker is released and is close to signing with Benfica]|url=http://odia.ig.com.br/esporte/flamengo/2017-07-11/atacante-do-flamengo-e-liberado-e-esta-proximo-de-assinar-com-o-benfica.html|publisher=Odia|accessdate=26 December 2017|language=Portuguese|date=11 July 2017}}</ref> Anjos joined Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica]] and was assigned to its [[S.L. Benfica B|reserve team]] on 22 July after agreeing to a five-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Daniel dos Anjos assina pelo Benfica [Daniel dos Anjos signs for Benfica]|url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/1a-liga/benfica/noticias/interior/daniel-dos-anjos-assina-pelo-benfica-8656165.html|publisher=Ojogo|accessdate=26 December 2017|language=Portuguese|date=22 July 2017}}</ref>

On 30 November 2020, dos Anjos tested positive for [[COVID-19]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=November 30, 2020|title=Daniel dos Anjos infected with Covid-19 – Benfica|url=https://www.time24.news/2020/11/daniel-dos-anjos-infected-with-covid-19-benfica.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=December 14, 2020|website=Time24}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and in subsequent medical tests post-recovery he was diagnosed with acute [[myocarditis]], which led him to temporarily suspend his career.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=December 13, 2020|title=Benfica striker who was bet by Jesus forced to suspend career due to heart problem – Observer|url=https://www.time24.news/2020/12/benfica-striker-who-was-bet-by-jesus-forced-to-suspend-career-due-to-heart-problem-observer.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=December 14, 2020|website=Time24}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On 21 August 2024, dos Anjos returned to Portugal and signed a three-year contract with [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=União de Leiria|url=https://www.uniaodeleiria.pt/uniao-de-leiria-reforca-ataque-com-daniel-dos-anjos/|title=União de Leiria reforça ataque com Daniel dos Anjos|trans-title=Leiria Union strengthens attack with Daniel dos Anjos|date=21 August 2024|access-date=19 September 2024|language=pt}}</ref>

On 31 July 2025, after a month on trial, dos Anjos signed for [[V.League 1]] club [[Ninh Binh FC|Ninh Binh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thethao247.vn/177936-tien-dao-brazil-tung-khoac-ao-benfica-gia-nhap-ninh-binh-fc-d379131.html|title=Tiền đạo Brazil từng khoác áo Benfica gia nhập Ninh Bình FC|publisher=Thể Thao 247|date=31 July 2025}}</ref>

In July 2026, dos Anjos moved to [[V.League 2]] club [[Becamex Ho Chi Minh City FC|Becamex Ho Chi Minh City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thethao247.vn/191838-tien-dao-brazil-roi-vleague-bat-ngo-xuong-choi-hang-nhat-d429467.html|title=Tiền đạo Brazil rời V.League, bất ngờ xuống chơi hạng Nhất|publisher=Thể Thao 247|date=13 July 2026}}</ref>
