'''Étienne Falgoux''' (born 19 January 1993) is a French [[rugby union|rugby union player]], currently playing in the [[Prop (rugby union)|prop]] for [[Top 14]] side [[ASM Clermont Auvergne|Clermont Auvergne]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Etienne Falgoux Profile|url=http://www.itsrugby.co.uk/player-30960.html|accessdate=23 February 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
Falgoux won his first cap for [[France national rugby union team|France]] as a replacement in the side's win over [[Scotland national rugby union team|Scotland]] in the [[2019 Six Nations Championship|2019 Six Nations]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rugby Union - ESPN Scrum - France vs Scotland at Stade de Francais |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/rugby/match?gameId=294252&league=180659 |website=ESPN.co.uk |accessdate=23 February 2019 |pages=Notes}}</ref>

==Club career==
In the [[2016–17 Top 14 season]], Falgoux won the championship, coming on as a substitute in the final win against Toulon.

'''Yuri Naves Roberto''' (born 7 October 1989), commonly known as '''Yuri''' and '''Yuri Naves''', is a Brazilian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

==Career==

A product of [[Atlético Mineiro]]'s youth academy, Naves played for several clubs throughout his career, most notably [[CS Marítimo]], [[Clube de Regatas Brasil|CRB]], and [[Vila Nova Futebol Clube|Vila Nova]]. He retired in 2022 while playing for Boston City Brasil.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.galodigital.com.br/enciclopedia/Yuri_Naves_Roberto |title=Yuri Naves Roberto |website=Galopédia |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Atletico_MG/0,,MUL1425477-9859,00.html |title=Tchô e Yuri trocam o Atlético-MG pelo Marítimo, de Portugal |website=GloboEsporte |date=23 December 2009 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/mg/sul-de-minas/futebol/times/boa-esporte/noticia/2012/02/emprestado-pelo-atletico-yuri-chega-e-ja-treina-no-boa-esporte.html |title=Emprestado pelo Atlético, Yuri chega e já treina no Boa Esporte |website=GloboEsporte |date=27 February 2012 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/go/futebol/times/vila-nova/noticia/vila-rescinde-contrato-com-yuri.ghtml |title=Vila rescinde contrato com Yuri |website=GloboEsporte |date=27 April 2021 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref> 

==Post-career==

Shortly after retiring, he became a scout for Boston City and was subsequently promoted to coordinator.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/mg/grande-minas-vales/noticia/2024/01/29/yuri-naves-deixa-o-boston-city-e-sera-coordenador-tecnico-do-vila-nova.ghtml |title=Yuri Naves deixa o Boston City e será coordenador técnico do Vila Nova |website=GloboEsporte |date=29 January 2024 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref>  Following the club's strong performance in the [[Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior]] (in partnership with Sãocarlense), Naves was hired by Vila Nova to coordinate its youth divisions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maisgoias.com.br/esportes/vila-nova-anuncia-ex-jogador-como-coordenador-das-categorias-de-base/ |title=Vila Nova anuncia ex-jogador como coordenador das categorias de base |website=Mais Goiás |date=24 January 2024 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref>  A year later, he was promoted to the club's general football coordinator, a position he held for one year. He is currently the coordinator for [[Nação Esportes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://opopular.com.br/esporte/por-que-yuri-naves-e-o-favorito-ao-cargo-de-diretor-de-futebol-no-vila-nova-1.3198952 |title=Por que Yuri Naves é o favorito ao cargo de diretor de futebol no Vila Nova |website=O Popular |date=13 November 2024 |access-date=21 August 2026 |language=pt }}</ref>

Mix Nine) |url=http://www.topstarnews.net/news/articleView.html?idxno=619831 |access-date=2021-03-11 |website=Top Star News |language=ko}} formerly known by her stage name '''Eyedi''' ({{Korean|아이디}}), is a South Korean singer-songwriter, composer, and actress. She debuted in 2016 under Bace Camp Studios with the self-written single "Sign" and released her first album, ''Mix B'', in 2017. Later that year, Nam participated on the survival reality show ''[[Mix Nine]]'', where she finished fifth out of the female contestants.{{Cite web |last=Cy |date=2019-12-30 |title="I Try to Show My Honest Self": An Interview with Retro-R&B Artist Eyedi |url=https://hiphopkr.com/interviews/interview-eyedi/ |access-date=2022-02-01 |website=HiphopKR |language=en-US}} In 2019, she was a cast member on the reality show ''Studio Vibes'', and was then cast as Lee Eun-byul in the web drama ''Thumbs Up Feeds Me'' (2020).{{Cite web|title=Eyedi to appear in new web drama 'Okay, I'll feed you'|url=https://www.allkpop.com/article/2020/06/eyedi-to-appear-in-new-web-drama-okay-ill-feed-you|access-date=2021-03-11|website=[[Allkpop]]|language=en}}{{Unreliable source?|reason=See reliable sources list on [[WP:KO/RS]]|date=June 2025}} She departed from Bace Camp Studios in 2024 following approximately four years of legal disputes. == Name == Nam derived her stage name "Eyedi" from ID (identity) in Korean, expressing her goal of people recognizing her when they listen to her music.{{Cite web|date=2018-07-08|title=INTERVIEW {{!}} Mix It Up With Eyedi|url=https://blog.onehallyu.com/interview-mix-it-up-with-eyedi/|access-date=2021-03-11|website=OH! Press|language=en-US|archive-date=April 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423221106/https://blog.onehallyu.com/interview-mix-it-up-with-eyedi/|url-status=dead}}{{Unreliable source?|reason=See reliable sources list on [[WP:KO/RS]]|date=June 2025}} In February 2024, Nam adopted her birth name, Nam Yu-jin, as her stage name, and announced that she would no longer use the name "Eyedi". == Career == === 2016–2017: Debut, ''Mix B'', and ''Mix Nine'' === Nam became interested in music and dreamed of becoming a singer after joining the singing club in her second year of high school; however, she also wanted to become a fashion designer since she enjoyed art. Nam made her debut on July 19, 2016, under Bace Camp Studios with the single "Sign", which she cowrote with [[Loopy (rapper)|Loopy]] and Francis and coproduced.{{Citation|script-title=ko:아이디(Eyedi) - Sign (Feat. Loopy)| date=July 18, 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yo-pHJYCgR4|language=en|access-date=2021-03-29}} She contacted Loopy after watching his [[YouTube]] videos prior to his debut, and they began working together. The music video for "Sign" was filmed in [[Los Angeles]], but the footage was lost and [[behind-the-scenes]] footage was used instead. On July 21, she attended 2016 International Fashion Week in Zhengzhou to perform "Sign" as well as "[[Firework (song)|Firework]]" by [[Katy Perry]]. She held her first fan signing event on July 23. Nam appeared on [[Seoul Broadcasting System|SBS Radio]] and performed a cover of "[[What You Do (Chrisette Michele song)|What You Do]]" by [[Chrisette Michele]].{{Citation|title=[SBS]최화정의파워타임, What You Do(원곡 Chrisette Michele ), 아이디 라이브|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FzrU7PJJSsM&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=128|language=en|access-date=2021-03-29}} On November 8, Nam released the single album ''Not Lonely'', including the title track "Not Lonely" and its instrumental version,{{Citation|title=Eyedi - 외롭지 않아|url=http://www.bainil.com/album/3387|language=en|access-date=2021-03-29|archive-date=October 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026110109/https://www.bainil.com/album/3387|url-status=dead}} as well as an acoustic version of "Sign",{{Citation|title=Sign (Acoustic Ver.) (Feat. Loopy)| date=June 16, 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sNSO20Suvxw|language=en|access-date=2021-03-29}} which she performed at the Acoustic X De Rêve Fashion Show'.{{Citation|script-title=ko:아이디(Eyedi) 'Sign(사인)' 어쿠스틱X드레브 패션쇼 콜라보 무대| date=December 4, 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0Dwoq4x2bM&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=127|language=en|access-date=2021-03-29}} On January 16, 2017, Nam released her third single album ''Chapter 21'', featuring Korean and English versions of the song "Type" and an instrumental version. The Korean version featured Kim Hyo-eun, who appeared on ''[[Show Me the Money 3]]'', and the English version featured [[Mario Winans]]. Nam announced the release of her song "Best Mistake" on March 17,{{Citation|title=[Teaser] Eyedi(아이디) - Best Mistake (K)| date=March 17, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MzHDvXmdidM&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=118|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} with the album name ''Mix B'' announced two days later with a teaser of the album uploaded. The album included a remastered version of "Sign" as well as five new tracks, of which the title track "Best Mistake" and "Falling" she wrote herself.{{Citation|title=Eyedi(아이디) The 1st Album [Mix B] Preview| date=March 19, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rLM94Y4KY0o&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=118|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} ''Mix B'' was released on March 21.{{Citation|title=Eyedi(아이디) - Best Mistake (K) Official Music Video| date=March 21, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uVC7EEEqlEs&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=116|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} Nam attended 2017 F/W Seoul Fashion Week.{{Citation|title=Eyedi(아이디) - 2017 FW Seoul Fashion Week| date=April 7, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P-MKm7bJoNY&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=113|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} On April 14, she had her first music show performance with "Best Mistake" on ''[[Show Champion]]''.{{Citation|title=Show Champion EP.224 EYEDI - Best Mistake| date=April 13, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=updBPXZbhJg|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} In June, Nam starred in her first commercial film for FUNPICK X Pikicast.{{Citation|title=Eyedi(아이디) - FUNPICK X Pikicast ad [2017.06.09.]| date=June 9, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0oQ5lb35pns&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=104|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} She held her second fan meeting on July 1.{{Citation|title=Eyedi(아이디) - FAN MEETING(UNION ART FAIR 2017) [2017.07.01.]| date=July 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bJ12zLsVvwk&list=PLQ_qQyOst1RQrsJOzVuPUywop38IZ1U-o&index=103|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} She released her first EP ''Tomorrowland'' on August 4 with the tracks "Tomorrowland" and "Dreamcatcher" along instrumentals for both tracks. "Tomorrowland" was written for a suicide prevention campaign, and Nam stated that she "ruminated on the lyrics as I wrote them in hopes of giving strength". On October 29, Nam and labelmate Jung Sa-ra auditioned for ''[[Mix Nine]]'' with "[[Spotlight (Jennifer Hudson song)|Spotlight]]" by [[Jennifer Hudson]]. In Episode 14, she ranked fifth, placing her in the debut line-up for the female team. However, the female team lost to the male team in the last episode, losing the opportunity to debut.{{Cite web |last=Ko |first=Daniel |date=2019-02-25 |title=Mixnine Final Rankings (Female Team) |url=https://www.playlive.fm/mixnine-final-rankings-female-team/ |access-date=2021-03-20 |website=PlayLive.fm |language=en-US}} She later stated that when she joined the show, she was under the impression that ''Mix Nine'' was a show for underrated artists to showcase their talent, not an [[Korean idol|idol program]], but found it a valuable experience and does not regret participating.{{Cite web |date=December 21, 2018 |title= |script-title=ko:[루키인터뷰 : 얘 어때?③] 아이디(Eyedi) "'믹스나인' 출연, 얻은 게 더 많은 값진 경험" |trans-title=[Rookie Interview: How is She?③] Eyedi "I gained more valuable experience from appearing on 'Mix Nine'" |url=https://sports.donga.com/3/all/20181222/93406521/2 |website=Sports DongA}} === 2018–2024: Debut in Japan, acting debut, and hiatus === Nam released her second EP ''Luv Highway'' with the title track of the same name and a second song "A Midsummer Night's Dream", as well as instrumentals for both tracks.{{Cite web|script-title=ko:아이디(Eyedi) [Luv Highway] 자켓 촬영 현장 공개 + 10문 10답|url=https://m.post.naver.com/viewer/postView.nhn?volumeNo=15673308&memberNo=4525616|access-date=2021-03-30|website=m.post.naver.com|language=ko}}{{Unreliable source?|reason=See reliable sources list on [[WP:KO/RS]]|date=June 2025}} She uploaded music videos for both songs. The "Luv Highway" music video was supposed to be shot in [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]], but the schedule coincided with the Japanese holidays so she was unable to film there.{{Cite web |date=2019-08-09 |title= |script-title=ja:日本オリジナル楽曲「Perfect 6th Sense」をリリースしたEyedi、自身の"6th Sense"とは |trans-title=Eyedi, who released the Japanese original song "Perfect 6th Sense", what is her "6th Sense"? |url=https://recochoku.jp/ch/recolog/2019_eyedi/ |access-date=2021-03-20 |website=Recochoku |language=ja}} The music video features Nam and [[Lee Jong-won (actor, born 1994)|Lee Jong-won]] as a couple on a date. She made her debut in Japan with an [[extended play]] under [[Pony Canyon]] titled ''coll[a]ction''. The release contained a Japanese version of "Sign" featuring Jinmenusagi, and its music video was shot in [[Tokyo]] with a focus on color{{Cite web |date=2018-07-23 |title= |script-title=ja:韓国のR&Bシンガー・Eyedi、Jinmenusagiとコラボした日本デビュー曲のMVティザー映像が公開 |trans-title=Korean R&B singer Eyedi releases MV teaser video for her Japanese debut song in collaboration with Jinmenusagi |url=https://spincoaster.com/news/eyedi-share-sing-japanese-ver-feat-jinmenusagi-mv-teaser-movie |access-date=2021-03-20 |website=Spincoaster |language=ja}} and released on August 10. The name ''coll[a]ction'' is a [[portmanteau]] of "collection" and "action", with the desire for the release to express the feeling of capturing Eyedi's songs.{{Cite web |title= |script-title=ja:Eyedi(アイディ)、日本ファースト・ミニ・アルバム『coll[a]ction』 |trans-title=Eyedi, first Japanese mini album ''coll[a]ction'' |url=https://tower.jp/article/feature_item/2018/08/29/0104 |access-date=2021-03-20 |website=Tower Records}} Nam released her fifth single "Red" on September 21 alongside a music video. "Red" was described as "jazz-style soul classic R&B that embodies a deeper and more vintage sound than a trendy style". Eyed was selected to perform at 2018 MU:CON in [[Seoul]].{{Cite web |last= |date=2018-09-21 |title= |script-title=ko:알앤비 퀸 아이디Eyedi 컴백 빈티지 사운드 RED 21일 발표 |trans-title=R&B queen Eyedi comeback vintage sound RED announced on the 21st |url=https://www.wowtv.co.kr/NewsCenter/News/Read?articleId=A201809210048 |access-date=2021-03-30 |website=Wow TV |language=ko}} On October 21, Nam held her first solo concert "The Red Station",{{Cite web |last= |date=2018-10-22 |title= |script-title=ko:아이디, 생애 첫 콘서트 성료…RED STATION '아이디X가은' 정상급 무대 눈길 |trans-title=Eyedi successfully completes her first concert... RED STATION 'Eyedi X Ga-eun' Top stage attention |url=http://biz.heraldcorp.com/culture/view.php?ud=201810221034548117889_1 |access-date=2021-03-30 |website=[[Herald Business]] |language=ko}} performing her songs and also covering "If You Let Me" by [[Sinéad Harnett]], "[[What You Do (Chrisette Michele song)|What You Do]]" by [[Chrisette Michele]], and "Have I Told You Lately" by [[Olivia Ong]]. Nam released "Caffeine" on December 17. On April 6, 2019, Nam released the single "&New".{{Citation|title=[M/V] Eyedi(아이디) - & New| date=April 26, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zElfR8e1iso|language=en|access-date=2021-03-30}} On June 6, Nam opened her [[YouTube]] channel Hey, Dream,{{Cite web|script-title=ko:해드림! Hey, Dream : 네이버TV|url=https://tv.naver.com/heydream|access-date=2021-03-28|website=[[Naver TV]]|language=ko}}{{Unreliable source?|reason=See reliable sources list on [[WP:KO/RS]]|date=June 2025}} where fans submit stories via comment and she selects a winner whom she contacts. Nam appeared on ''[[Studio Vibes]]'', covering "[[Make You Feel My Love]]" by [[Bob Dylan]] with another participant.{{Citation| date=June 19, 2019 |script-title=ko:[미공개 영상(tvN 작업실)] 아이디, 최낙타 - Make You Feel My Love|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FlWyfy_M3oI|language=en|access-date=2021-03-28}} She later released her second Japanese single "Perfect 6th Sense" with the intention of awakening the [[Extrasensory perception|sixth sense]] with the music. It was described as depicting "the liberation of oneself to challenge music". Nam was involved in the songwriting, composition, and production process.{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2019 |title= |script-title=ja:韓国R&BシンガーソングライターEyedi(アイディ)、初の日本オリジナル曲を配信リリース |trans-title=Korean R&B singer-songwriter Eyedi releases her first Japanese original song |url=https://www.barks.jp/news/?id=1000170007 |access-date=2021-03-20 |website=Barks |language=ja}} The music video was released on August 5, and Nam commented that it was "flashier" than her previous music videos, and the highlight was the colors used. On December 8, 2019, Nam participated in the MU:CON collaboration track "7UP",{{Citation|title=7UP| date=December 8, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jwMJuUxLd6A|language=en|access-date=2021-04-08}} helping write and compose the track alongside Kevin Wild of [[Bad Royale]] and others. The song was described as [[electronica]] and pop, with the bass rhythm and drum loop adding "a dreamy atmosphere".{{citation needed|date=September 2024}} On March 13, 2020, Nam released her tenth single "J.usT". On December 8, following a hiatus, she posted a snippet of a song, captioned to be released in 2021. Nam returned to YouTube on March 5, 2021, announcing that she would be continuing "Hey, Dream". However, there were no updates following the announcement. On July 10, 2022, the CEO of Bace Camp Studios stated that Eyedi was on indefinite hiatus.{{Cite web |url=https://twitter.com/eyediupdate/status/1546187339491319809 |access-date=2022-11-24 |website=Twitter |language=en}} === 2024–2026: Departure from label and retirement === On February 19, 2024, Nam announced through [[KakaoTalk]] that she had departed from Bace Camp Studio following approximately four years of legal disputes, and that she would continue her career under her birth name, Nam Yu-jin.{{cite web |url=https://x.com/YuJinUpdate/status/1759567688190361784 |title=x.com |website=x.com |access-date=2026-04-02}} On February 13, 2026, Nam announced her marriage through [[KakaoTalk]], and that she was retiring from the public eye.{{cite web |url=https://x.com/YuJinUpdate/status/2022435779608187008 |title=x.com |website=x.com |access-date=2026-08-22}} == Artistry == === Influences === Nam has named [[Stevie Wonder]] and [[Beyoncé]] as influences, and lists [[Lee Su-hyun]] from [[AKMU]], [[Taemin]] from [[Shinee]], and [[Jay Park]] as artists she would like to collaborate with.{{Citation |title=[Pops in Seoul] LIVE ATTACK with Eyedi(아이디)! Red / Luv Highway | date=October 19, 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueEPyomSk_c |access-date=2021-03-30 |language=en}} === Songwriting === Nam began composing prior to her debut, and she began to compose more of her releases after receiving recognition for "Tomorrowland" from the head of her agency. Her songwriting is influenced by colors, such as her single "Red", and she draws inspiration from sunsets and art galleries. === Fashion === Nam has expressed interest in fashion and has stated that 90% of the props and clothes used in her music videos are from her collection.{{Cite web |date=2020-05-02 |title= |script-title=ko:아이디는 언제나 봄 |trans-title=Eyedi is always spring |url=https://woman.donga.com/3/all/12/2050378/1 |access-date=2021-10-02 |website=Women's Donga |language=ko}} == Discography == === Studio albums === {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;" ! scope="col" rowspan="2" style="width:10em;"| Title ! scope="col" rowspan="2" | Album details ! scope="col" colspan="1" style="width:5em;" | Peak chart positions ! scope="col" rowspan="2" | Sales |- ! '''Mordechai Shapiro''' (born December 9, 1989) is an American singer-songwriter and entertainer in the [[Orthodox pop music|Orthodox pop]] industry. Jewish music producer Yitzy Waldner said that he has an  "ability to do things with his voice no one else in this business can".<ref name="5tjt">{{cite news |last1=Maruch Miller |first1=Rochelle |title=Critic's Choice: 'Machar' By Mordechai Shapiro |url=http://www.5tjt.com/critics-choice-machar-mordechai-shapiro/ |accessdate=9 June 2020 |work=The 5 Towns Jewish Times |date=4 October 2017}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Mordechai Shapiro was born on December 9, 1989 in [[Monsey, New York|Monsey]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. His father was a [[chazzan]] and his mother had a background as a trained opera singer. Growing up in a [[Modern Orthodox Judaism|Modern Orthodox]] household, he attended {{url|https://ashar.org|The Adolph Schreiber Hebrew Academy of Rockland}} for grade school, and the [[Marsha Stern Talmudical Academy]] for high school. Following his graduation from high school, Shapiro learned in [[yeshiva]] in [[Yeshivat Netiv Aryeh|Yeshiva Netiv Aryeh]] and [[Yeshivas Bais Yisroel]].<ref name="Mishpacha">{{cite news |last1=Besser |first1=Yisroel |title=We Can All Sing |url=https://mishpacha.com/we-can-all-sing/ |access-date=June 9, 2020|work=Mishpacha Magazine |date=12 March 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201208033939/https://mishpacha.com/we-can-all-sing/|archive-date=December 8, 2020}}</ref>

In 2010, Shapiro married Raquel Guenoun.<ref name="Mishpacha" />

== Career ==
Shapiro made his musical debut in 1997 as the star soloist of the [[Miami Boys Choir]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mordechai Shapiro to Perform at NCSY Gala |url=https://ncsy.org/mordechai-shapiro-perform-ncsy-gala/ |publisher=NCSY |accessdate=9 June 2020 |language=en |date=31 October 2017}}</ref> As a child, he performed with Jewish entertainers such as [[Yaakov Shwekey]] even before he gained significant attention.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mordechai Shapiro Then And Now |url=http://www.gruntig.net/2011/11/mordechai-shapiro-then-and-now.html |publisher=Gruntig |accessdate=9 June 2020 |date=9 November 2011}}</ref> He left Miami Boys Choir in 2003<ref name="mostly">{{cite web |title=Mordechai Shapiro - Kol Haderech |url=https://mostlymusic.com/products/mordechai-shapiro-kol-haderech |publisher=Mostly Music |accessdate=9 June 2020 |language=en |date=2016}}</ref> when his voice became too deep to fit into a children's choir.<ref name="allmusic">{{cite web |last1=Jurek |first1=Thom |title=Mordechai Shapiro Biography & History |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mordechai-shapiro-mn0003497232/biography#:~:text=Mordechai%20Shapiro%20is%20a%20New,on%20the%20Jewish%20music%20scene.&text=Shapiro%20was%20born%20in%20Monsey,and%20mother%20are%20both%20singers. |publisher=AllMusic |accessdate=9 June 2020 |language=en-us}}</ref>

After leaving the choir, Shapiro took a break from music until his voice transitioned sufficiently. He was a student of voice teacher William Riley, who also taught [[Celine Dion]] and [[Josh Groban]].<ref name="allmusic" /> Eventually, he began performing at weddings and other Jewish events as an independent artist.<ref name="mostly" />

Shapiro's solo career debuted in 2016 when he was signed by producer Yitzy Waldner, with the release of his album ''Kol Haderech'', peaking at #15 on the [[Billboard charts#Albums|Billboard]] World Music chart.<ref name="billboard">{{cite web |title=Mordechai Shapiro |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/mordechai-shapiro/chart-history |publisher=Billboard |accessdate=9 June 2020}}</ref> The album was followed by ''Machar'' in 2017, peaking at #3,<ref name="billboard" /> and ''Hakol Mishamayim'' in 2019, peaking at #7.<ref name="billboard" /> Shapiro is also known for his extravagant music videos- often including elaborate sets and dancers, showcasing his larger than life personality. His hit video for ''"Hakol Mishamayim"'' sits at 14 Million views on YouTube.<ref>{{Citation |title=MORDECHAI SHAPIRO - Hakol Mishamayim (Official Music Video) הכל משמים - מרדכי שפירא |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JN5AVdAzmzU |language=en |access-date=2022-05-31}}</ref> ''Hakol Mishamayim'' was filmed by Shimmy Socol, alongside ''Machar, Friends, Ein Od Milvado,'' also filmed by Socol.

Shapiro has cited [[Frank Sinatra]], [[Michael Jackson]] and [[Michael Bublé]] as his musical influences.<ref name="5tjt" />

'''Ana Carolina Vilela da Costa''' (born 6 February 1998) is a Brazilian singer-songwriter, best known for the song "Trem Bala".<ref name="Conheça">{{cite web|access-date=12 September 2017|author=Heloisa Tolipan|title=Conheça Ana Vilela, cantora e compositora de Trem Bala, música que já foi cantada por Gisele Bundchen e Luan Santana|url=http://www.heloisatolipan.com.br/musica/conheca-ana-vilela-cantora-e-compositora-de-trem-bala-musica-que-ja-foi-cantada-por-gisele-bundchen-e-luan-santana/}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> She became internationally known after her song "Trem Bala" became a viral phenomenon on the Internet, and her first national network performance during the program Caldeirão do Huck, where Ana partnered with Luan Santana.

==Biography==
Born in [[Londrina]], Vilela approached music as an adolescent, learning to play the guitar and composing at 12 years old.<ref name="Gazeta">{{cite news |last1=Gonçalves |first1=Juliana |title=Ana Vilela conta que Trem Bala ajuda a superar os traumas da vida |url=https://clube.gazetadopovo.com.br/noticias/outros/ana-vilela-conta-que-trem-bala-ajuda-a-superar-os-traumas-da-vida/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[Gazeta do Povo]] |date=13 September 2017 |language=pt-BR}}</ref> She had her breakout in 2016, when a clip of her song "Trem Bala" ('Bullet Train') went viral through YouTube and [[WhatsApp]], collecting in a short time millions of views.<ref name="Gazeta" /><ref name="bio1">{{cite news |title=Ana Vilela |url=https://dicionariompb.com.br/artista/ana-vilela/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[Dicionário Cravo Albin da Música Popular Brasileira]]}}</ref><ref name="bio">{{cite news |last1=Fonseca |first1=Alana |title=Autora paranaense de hit cantado por Gisele Bündchen diz que vive sonho |url=https://g1.globo.com/pr/parana/musica/noticia/2017/01/autora-paranaense-de-hit-cantado-por-gisele-bundchen-diz-que-vive-sonho.html |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[O Globo]] |date=22 January 2017 |language=pt-br}}</ref> The success of the song was increased when model [[Gisele Bündchen]] posted a cover of the song on Instagram.<ref name="Gazeta" /><ref name="bio1" />
The song was eventually officially released in 2017, in an EP which included two versions of the song, one of them in a duet with [[Luan Santana]].<ref name="bio1" /> The same year Virela released her first self-titled album, which was eventually nominated for [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Portuguese Language Contemporary Pop Album|Best Portuguese Language Contemporary Pop Album]] at the [[19th Annual Latin Grammy Awards]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Redação |title=Paranaense Ana Vilela é indicada ao Grammy Latino |url=https://www.bemparana.com.br/cultura/paranaense-ana-vilela-e-indicada-ao-grammy-latino/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=Bem Paraná |date=20 September 2018 |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2018, Vivela released an EP of cover versions of [[Sertanejo music|sertanejo]] songs, and her composition "Promete" became the theme song of the telenovela ''[[Espelho da Vida]]''.<ref name="bio1" /> She released her second album, ''Contato'', in 2019.<ref name="bio1" /> In 2023, she released the album ''Melhor Que Ontem''.<ref name="Jornal">{{cite news |last1=Costa |first1=Ingrid |title=Em entrevista, Ana Vilela fala sobre novo álbum, "Melhor Que Ontem" |url=https://jornaldebrasilia.com.br/entretenimento/musica/em-entrevista-ana-vilela-fala-sobre-novo-album-melhor-que-ontem/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=Jornal de Brasília |date=2 June 2023 |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ana Vilela chora ao contar que conseguiu compor novamente após 2 anos: 'Volta por cima' |url=https://gshow.globo.com/tudo-mais/pop/noticia/ana-vilela-chora-ao-conseguir-voltar-a-compor-apos-2-anos-volta-por-cima.ghtml |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=O Globo |date=2 June 2023 |language=pt-br}}</ref> The same year, she joined the platform [[OnlyFans]].<ref name="Jornal" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Oliveira |first1=Fábia |title=Ana Vilela revela o que está por trás do seu Onlyfans |url=https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/fabia-oliveira/ana-vilela-revela-o-que-esta-por-tras-do-seu-onlyfans |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[Metrópoles]] |date=28 May 2023 |language=pt}}</ref>

== Career ==
Taking an interest in acting as a teenager, Kamio decided to quit his high school soccer club and began his acting career. As he was a fan of [[Hideaki Itō]], he auditioned for the same agency and passed,<ref name="signal">{{Cite web |date=2018-05-01 |script-title=ja:神尾楓珠インタビュー「兄弟の絆も見どころです」『シグナル 長期未解決事件捜査班』 |trans-title=Fuju Kamio Interview "Brotherly bonds are also a highlight" "Signal Long-Term Unsolved Case Investigation Team" |url=https://www.tvlife.jp/pickup/169384 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230816181825/https://www.tvlife.jp/pickup/169384 |archive-date=2023-08-16 |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=TV LIFE web |language=ja}}</ref> although Itō would later leave the agency in 2022.{{cn|date=May 2024}}

In the same year in 2015, Kamio made his television debut in ''Mother, I'm Fine'', a drama special for ''24Hour Television: Love Saves the Earth''.

He starred as Aran Maki, the 17-year-old prime minister of an experimental city, in ''[[Teen Regime]]'', reuniting with [[Anna Yamada]], whom he costarred with in ''[[Kanojo ga Suki na Mono wa Homo de Atte Boku de wa Nai|What She Likes...]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-11 |title= |script-title=ja:神尾楓珠：NHKドラマ初主演で17歳の若き総理に 共演に山田杏奈、星野源 脚本は吉田玲子 |trans-title=Fuju Kamio: 17-year-old young prime minister in first lead role in NHK drama Co-starring Anna Yamada and Gen Hoshino Screenplay by Reiko Yoshida |url=https://mantan-web.jp/article/20220111dog00m200044000c.html |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=Mantan Web |language=ja-JP}}</ref><ref name="kanojo" />

In May 2021, he made his first starring role in short film, "10 Years wondering in Shibuya - A Decade of Roaming" <ref>{{Cite web |title=神尾楓珠主演、短編映画『10年、渋谷をさ迷って』 本編映像公開 |url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2185291/full/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=ORICON NEWS}}</ref>

Kamio announced he had left his agency on December 31, 2023.{{cn|date=May 2024}}

For the [[2020-21 NL season|2020–21 season]], Jäger returned to Switzerland and the NL, joining [[Lausanne HC]].{{cite web |title=Ken Jäger profile |website=Eurohockey.com |date=11 May 2025 |url=https://www.eurohockey.com/player/580870-ken-jger.html |access-date=11 May 2025}} In September 2022, he signed a contract extension with the LHC lasting until the end of the 2025–26 season.{{cite web |last=Gauci |first=Antoine |title=Ken Jäger Prolonge son contrat de 3 saisons avec le LHC |website=Lausanne HC |date=14 September 2022 |url=https://lausannehc.ch/2022/09/14/ken-jager-prolonge-son-contrat-de-3-saisons-avec-le-lhc/ |language=fr |access-date=12 May 2025}} In August 2025, Jäger signed a seven-year contract with [[HC Davos]], returning to the team starting with the [[2025-26 National League (ice hockey) season|2026–27 season]] until 2033.{{cite web |title=HCD verpflichtet Ken Jäger ab der Saison 2026/27 |website=Hockey Club Davos |url=https://www.hcd.ch/de/news/hcd-verpflichtet-ken-jaeger-ab-der-saison-202627 |language=de |access-date=2025-09-09}} ==International play== {{MedalTableTop|name=}} {{MedalCountry|{{ih|SUI}}}} {{MedalSport|[[Ice hockey]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Ice Hockey World Championships|World Championships]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2024 IIHF World Championship|2024 Czechia]]|}} {{MedalSilver|[[2025 IIHF World Championship|2025 Sweden/Denmark]]|}} {{MedalSilver|[[2026 IIHF World Championship|2026 Switzerland]]|}} {{MedalBottom}} Jäger was named to [[Switzerland men's national junior ice hockey team|Switzerland's under-20 team]] for the [[2018 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]]. '''Vasiliοs Labropoulos''' ({{langx|el|Βασίλειος Λαμπρόπουλος}}; born 31 March 1990) is a Greek professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]].<ref name="kicker">{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/vassilis-lampropoulos/spieler/|language=de|title=Vassilis Lampropoulos|publisher=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]]|access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref><ref name="worldfootball">{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe161555/vassilios-lampropoulos/ |title=Vasilios Lampropoulos|website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL|access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==
Labropoulos was born in [[Pyrgos, Elis|Pyrgos]] on 31 March 1990, and he has played for [[Apollon Kalamarias F.C.|Apollon Kalamarias]], [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]], [[GS Ilioupoli|Ilioupoli]], [[Ethnikos Asteras F.C.|Ethnikos Asteras]], and [[Panionios F.C.|Panionios]].

On 24 January 2014, Labropoulos decided to continue his career to [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] in the [[Football League]], starting the [[2013–14 Football League (Greece)|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/gethniki/aek/phre-kai-lampropoylo-h-aek.2609722.html|script-title=el:Πήρε και Λαμπρόπουλο η ΑΕΚ|publisher=contra.gr|language=el|access-date=24 January 2014|archive-date=27 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140127011813/http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/gethniki/aek/phre-kai-lampropoylo-h-aek.2609722.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 8 April 2017, Labropoulos ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in a [[Super League]] game against [[Platanias F.C.|Platanias]] and underwent a successful surgery, while his comeback was estimated in around six months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zougla.gr/sports/podosfero/aek/article/aek-xirourgi8ike-epitixos-o-lampropoulos |script-title=el:ΑΕΚ: Χειρουργήθηκε επιτυχώς ο Λαμπρόπουλος |publisher=zougla.gr |language=el| access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref> In his day of surgery, Lampropoulos extended his contract with the [[Greek Cup]] winners by two years, despite being ruled out for six months with a knee injury. The 27-year-old's contract had been due to expire in the summer of 2017, but that has been stretched to 2019 by his club. Lampropoulos always had the desire to remain at AEK Athens and he was more than happy to commit his future to the club for the next two years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/omades/Aek/symfwnia-ths-aek-me-lampropoylo-mpakakh-gia-neo-symvolaio.4616859.html |script-title=el:Συμφωνία της ΑΕΚ με Λαμπρόπουλο-Μπακάκη για νέο συμβόλαιο! |publisher=sport24.gr |language=el| access-date=8 April 2017}}</ref>

On 12 April 2017, Labropoulos agreed to a contract extension with AEK, until the summer of 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/article/1070938/ananeose-me-aek-o-lampropoylos-eos-2020|title=Ανανέωσε ο Λαμπρόπουλος!|access-date=12 April 2017|language=el}}</ref>

On 26 November 2018, despite the fact that he was a key figure for the club{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}, following the Super League defeat from [[Panetolikos F.C.|Panetolikos]], AEK owner [[Dimitris Melissanidis]] engaged in a heated conversation with three players, ostracizing Lampropoulos, [[André Simões]] and [[Anastasios Bakasetas]] from the team.'' "For Simoes, Labropoulos and Bakasetas, who have not agreed to sign a new contract, we will search for options to allow them to leave in January".'' said the owner of the club. In his press conference ahead of the upcoming Champions League game against [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], head coach [[Marinos Ouzounidis]] practically confirmed that the trio would not be a part of his team anymore:'' "These guys have helped the team a lot, but since we talked and couldn’t reach an agreement, it’s probably best for the club to make a decision".'' Unless Lampropoulos, Simoes and Bakasetas all suddenly decided to pen a new deal with AEK, they would not play for the club again. Last season, a similar situation developed with goalkeeper [[Giannis Anestis]], who was subsequently ostracized from the team after refusing to extend his contract.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fosonline.gr/podosfairo/champions-league/article/31659/toys-teleiosan-ektos-apostolis-me-agiax-oi-mpakasetas-lampropoylos-simoes|title=Τους τέλειωσαν: Εκτός αποστολής με Άγιαξ οι Μπακασέτας, Λαμπρόπουλος, Σιμόες |access-date=26 November 2018|language=el}}</ref>

On 27 June 2019, [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] confirmed the signing of Labropoulos on a free transfer for the next two seasons. Deportivo missed out on promotion to [[La Liga]], [[2018–19 La Liga|this year]] after losing to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] in the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/diethnes-podosfairo/epishmo-sth-nteportivo-o-lampropoylos.5546565.html |title=Επίσημο: Στη Ντεπορτίβο ο Λαμπρόπουλος |access-date=27 June 2019|language=el}}</ref>

On 31 January 2020, Labropoulos joined [[VfL Bochum]] on loan until the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vfl-bochum.de/news/uebersicht/profis/lampropoulos-auf-leihbasis-zum-vfl/|title=Lampropoulos auf Leihbasis zum VfL|language=de|publisher=VfL Bochum|date=31 January 2020}}</ref> On 14 August 2020, he has signed a two-year contract with VfL Bochum of the [[2. Bundesliga]]. The 30-year-old centre-back had been on loan at Bochum from Deportivo during the second half of the previous campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vfl-bochum.de/news/uebersicht/profis/vfl-holt-lampropoulos/|title=VfL holt Lampropoulos|language=de|publisher=VfL Bochum|date=14 August 2020|access-date=20 August 2020|archive-date=14 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814182804/https://www.vfl-bochum.de/news/uebersicht/profis/vfl-holt-lampropoulos/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 15 December 2020, he faced a muscle injury in a game against [[Hannover 96]] and he estimated to be in the injury list for at least four months. At the end of the season VfL Bochum were crowned champions of 2. Bundesliga and promoted to [[Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/2020-21-promotion-run-in-hamburg-bochum-holstein-kiel-fortuna-dusseldorf-15293 |title=Bundesliga 2: how promotion was decided on the final day |language=en|publisher=bundesliga.com |date=23 May 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
On 9 November 2018, Greece new coach [[Angelos Anastasiadis]] called up Labropoulos for the match against [[Finland national football team|Finland]] and [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]] for [[UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/ethniki_elladas/ethnikh-elladas-oi-prwtes-klhseis-toy-aggeloy-anastasiadh.5359053.html|title=Εθνική Ελλάδας: Οι πρώτες κλήσεις του Άγγελου Αναστασιάδη|language=el|date=10 November 2018|archive-date=11 November 2018|access-date=17 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111043644/https://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/ethniki_elladas/ethnikh-elladas-oi-prwtes-klhseis-toy-aggeloy-anastasiadh.5359053.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 15 November 2018, he made his debut in a 1–0 home win game against [[Finland national football team|Finland]].

'''Lucas Eduardo Carrizo''' (born 20 May 1997) is an Argentine [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for [[Newell's Old Boys]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucas Carrizo Stats {{!}} Soccerway |url=https://www.soccerway.com/player/carrizo-lucas/Uaa9q5tS/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=www.soccerway.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Carrizo came through the youth setup at [[Quilmes Atlético Club|Quilmes]], where he made his debut on 10 May 2017 in the [[Copa Argentina]] in a penalty shootout loss to [[Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza|Gimnasia Mendoza.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quilmes debuta en la Copa Argentina |url=https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/1054/23009/quilmes-debuta-en-la-copa-argentina |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=El Gráfico |language=es}}</ref> On 17 July 2018, he signed for [[Primera B Metropolitana]] club [[Club Atlético San Telmo|San Telmo]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Llegó, Lucas Carrizo |url=https://www.soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=909 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123153727/https://www.soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=909 |archive-date=2021-11-23 |access-date=2026-02-17 |work=Club Atlético San Telmo |language=es-ES}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 29 April 2019 in a 2–1 win against [[Estudiantes de Buenos Aires|Estudiantes BA]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Subido a una ilusion |url=https://soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1136&cat=1&div=1&a=79 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240304221951/https://soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1136&cat=1&div=1&a=79 |archive-date=2024-03-04 |access-date=2026-02-17 |work=Club Atlético San Telmo |language=es-ES}}</ref>

On 7 July 2019, he signed for [[Primera Nacional]] club [[Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza|Gimnasia Mendoza]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=club atlético san telmo |url=http://soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1218 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820212047/http://soydetelmo.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1218 |archive-date=2019-08-20 |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=www.soydetelmo.com.ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gimnasia (Mendoza): “Quiero pelear cosas importantes” |url=https://www.soloascenso.com.ar/notas/gimnasia-y-esgrima-mendoza/quiero-pelear-cosas-importantes/135762 |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=www.soloascenso.com.ar |language=es}}</ref> In August 2020, he signed a new contract until June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-08-24 |title=El Tucu Carrizo renovó su vínculo con Gimnasia |url=https://www.diariouno.com.ar/ovacion/futbol/tucu-carrizo-renovo-vinculo-gimnasia-08242020_ffs-fFAmf |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=Diario Uno |language=es}}</ref> On April 8 2021, he scored the winning goal in a 2–1 win against [[Club Atlético Alvarado|Alvarado]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-08 |title=Lucas Carrizo y su alegría doble por el triunfo de Gimnasia |url=https://www.diariouno.com.ar/ovacion/futbol/lucas-carrizo-y-su-alegria-doble-el-triunfo-gimnasia-n823279 |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=Diario Uno |language=es}}</ref> He returned to the Liga Profesional in 2022 as he joined [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]] on loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-04 |title=¡Llegaron los primeros dos refuerzos! {{!}} Huracán |url=https://cahuracan.com/noticias/llegaron-los-primeros-dos-refuerzos |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=cahuracan.com |language=es}}</ref> After the 2023 season ended, he signed for the club permanently.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-09 |title=Huracán compró a Lucas Carrizo {{!}} Huracán |url=https://cahuracan.com/noticias/huracan-compro-a-lucas-carrizo |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=cahuracan.com |language=es}}</ref> On 13 April 2024, he scored twice in a 4–0 win against [[Atlético Tucumán]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-04-13 |title=Lucas Carrizo impulsó la victoria de Huracán frente a Atlético Tucumán con dos goles |url=https://www.futbolred.com/otras-ligas-de-futbol/lucas-carrizo-impulso-la-victoria-de-huracan-frente-a-atletico-tucuman-con-dos-goles-207556 |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=futbolred.com |language=spanish}}</ref> On 29 October, the club confirmed that Carrizo suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury in a match against [[Central Córdoba de Santiago del Estero|Central Córdoba SdE]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Modini |first=Tomás |date=2024-10-29 |title=Huracán y una muy mala noticia: Lucas Carrizo se rompió los ligamentos |url=https://www.vermouth-deportivo.com.ar/huracan-y-una-muy-mala-noticia-lucas-carrizo-se-rompio-los-ligamentos/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=Vermouth Deportivo |language=es}}</ref> He made his return in a reserve game on 20 May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Carrizo volvió en Reserva y convirtió {{!}} Huracán |url=https://cahuracan.com/noticias/carrizo-volvio-en-reserva-y-convirtio |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=cahuracan.com |language=es}}</ref>

'''Arman T. Shields''' (born July 10, 1985) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond Spiders]], and was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fourth round of the [[2008 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Arman T. Shields was born on July 10, 1985.<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/s/shie00300.html#gsc.tab=0 | title=Arman Shields | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Gonzaga College High School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name="Pfa"/>

==College career==
Shield played [[college football]] for the [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond Spiders]] of the [[University of Richmond]] from 2004 to 2007.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was [[redshirted]] in 2003.<ref name="Pfa"/> He earned second-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] honors in 2006 after catching five touchdowns.<ref name="Sign">{{cite web | url=https://richmondspiders.com/sports/2008/7/24/205205994 | title=Arman Shields Signs With Oakland | publisher=[[University of Richmond]] | date=July 24, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref> As a senior in 2007, he recorded 12 receptions for 107 yards in the season opener.<ref name="Packett">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch/194063115/ | title=A chance from Santa | work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] | date=February 20, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=Packett, John | pages=C2}}</ref> However, he suffered a [[torn PCL]] the next week.<ref name="Packett"/> He briefly returned for one [[Series (American football)|series]] in an October game before missing the rest of the season due to the injury.<ref name="Packett"/> Shields finished his college career with 160 catches for 1,930 yards and 13 touchdowns.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tribune/194063041/ | title=Raiders trade away Washington | work=[[The Tribune (San Luis Obispo)|The Tribune]] | date=April 28, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | pages=S3}}</ref> His receptions total was the second most in school history.<ref name="Combine">{{cite web | url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2008/2/29/205202115 | title=Arman Shields Puts Up Big Numbers At 2008 NFL Combine | publisher=[[University of Richmond]] | date=February 29, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Shields was the first Richmond player invited to the [[NFL Combine]] since [[Shawn Barber (American football)|Shawn Barber]] in 1998.<ref name="Packett"/> Shields was one of the fastest players at the Combine, posting a 4.37 second [[40-yard dash]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-free-lance-star/194063463/ | title=More state players chosen | work=[[The Free Lance-Star]] | date=April 28, 2008 | agency=[[Associated Press]] | accessdate=23 March 2026 | pages=B2}}</ref> He had the best [[20-yard shuttle]] (3.96 s) and the best 60-yard shuttle (10.87 s).<ref name="Combine"/> He was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fourth round, with the 125th overall pick, of the [[2008 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee/194063564/ | title=Washington is traded to Ravens | work=[[The Sacramento Bee]] | date=April 28, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=Jones, Jason | pages=C6}}</ref> ''[[The Daytona Beach News-Journal]]'' noted that Shields was a "surprising choice after fewer than 2,000 career yards and a serious injury."<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daytona-beach-news-journal/194063650/ | title=AFC Draft Scorecard | work=[[The Daytona Beach News-Journal]] | date=April 28, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=Chapman, Alex | pages=3B}}</ref> The ''[[Oakland Tribune]]'' said that Shields was a "typical boom-or-bust, 'measurables' pick by owner [[Al Davis]]",<ref name="nbc">{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/arman-shields/00000188-9cf0-da6b-abd8-fcfd44df0045/news | title=Arman Shields | publisher=[[NBC Sports]] | accessdate=24 March 2026}}</ref> who was known for drafting fast players.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil |author-link=Gil Brandt |date=April 30, 2011 |title=Few recognize value of speed more than Raiders' Davis |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/few-recognize-value-of-speed-more-than-raiders-davis-09000d5d81f9b25d |accessdate=24 March 2026 |publisher=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2014/05/04/nfl-draft-raiders-obsession-with-speed-slowed-their-progress/ | title=NFL draft: Raiders’ obsession with speed slowed their progress | work=[[The Mercury News]] | date=May 4, 2014 | accessdate=24 March 2026 | author=Wilner, Jon}}</ref>

Shields missed most of spring practices in 2008 with a lower body injury.<ref name="nbc"/> He signed with the Raiders on July 23, 2008.<ref name="Sign"/> Davis gave Shields a $425K signing bonus.<ref name="nbc"/> On August 30, 2008, Shields was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury.<ref name="Pfa"/> He ended up missing the entire [[2008 NFL season]].<ref name="Pfa"/> On May 9, 2009, it was reported that Shields had not yet fully recovered from the injury.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/san-francisco-chronicle/194063932/ | title=Walker surprised team with surgery | work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] | date=May 9, 2009 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=White, David | pages=D8}}</ref> He was released by the Raiders on July 29, 2009, after failing a physical.<ref name="Pfa"/> In May 2010, he participated in rookie [[minicamp]] on a tryout basis with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref name="nbc"/>

==Personal life==
Shields' father, Bertie Shields, was a Guyanan immigrant who served in the [[United States Army]].<ref name="Carpenter">{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/2008/04/23/a-son-a-chance-a-dream/e38a3197-172d-4f3c-949e-1db5a08d607b/ | title=A Son, a Chance, a Dream | work=[[The Washington Post]] | date=April 22, 2008 | accessdate=24 March 2026 | author=Carpenter, Les}}</ref> While stationed in South Korea in 1975, he was tasked with walking one mile through the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone]] to spy through the fence.<ref name="Carpenter"/> Arman Shields became a real estate agent after his football career.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.desertlionproperty.com/arman-shields | title=Arman Shields | publisher=Desert Lion Property | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Bruno Gadiol Antoniassi''' (born 6 June 1998) is a Brazilian actor and singer. In 2013, he became known after winning the talent show on the program ''[[TV Xuxa]]'', which formed the group KidX. In 2016, he was a semi-finalist on the [[The Voice Brasil season 5|fifth season]] of the talent show ''[[The Voice Brasil]]''. In 2017, he made his acting debut as Guto in the twenty-fifth season of ''[[Malhação]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gshow.globo.com/novelas/malhacao/2017/personagem/guto/|title=Guto {{!}} Personagem {{!}} Gshow|access-date=14 September 2017|website=Gshow|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Bruno was born on 6 June 1998 in the [[Paraíso (São Paulo)|Paraíso]] neighborhood of [[São Paulo]].<ref name="purepeople">{{cite web|url=http://www.purepeople.com.br/famosos/bruno-gadiol_p548464|title=Bruno Gadiol|website=Purepeople|language=pt-BR}}</ref> At age eleven, his family moved to a condominium in [[Barueri]], and he began attending Colégio Samarah in the neighboring city of [[Cotia]].<ref name="baruerinarede">{{cite web|url=http://baruerinarede.com.br/bruno-gadiol-a-voz-que-tem-encantado-o-brasil/|title=Bruno Gadiol, "A Voz" que tem encantado o Brasil|website=Barueri na Rede|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2012, he formed the band Listras da Lombada with friends, performing pop and rock music at local events and music festivals.<ref name="baruerinarede"/> That same year, he starred in the plays ''[[The Wonderful Wizard of Oz|O Mágico de Oz]]'' and an adaptation of ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]''.<ref name="purepeople"/>

== Career ==
In March 2013, at age fourteen, Gadiol auditioned for a talent show on ''[[TV Xuxa]]'' hosted by [[Xuxa]], which aimed to form a mixed-gender group of teenagers who could sing and dance, inspired by international acts such as [[S Club 7]] and [[A*Teens]]. The competition received 2,000 applicants from across Brazil.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://inscricaonatv.com/2013/03/23/inscricao-no-concurso-de-cantores-da-xuxa-kidx/|title=Inscrição no concurso de cantores da Xuxa - Kidx|website=Inscrição na TV|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref> On 3 August 2013, after three months of auditions and workshops, he was announced as one of the chosen members of the group KidX.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gshow.globo.com/programas/tv-xuxa/O-Programa/noticia/2013/07/reveja-os-11-finalistas-que-continuam-na-disputa-do-kidx-e-prepare-sua-torcida.html|title=Reveja os 11 finalistas que continuam na disputa do KidX e prepare sua torcida!|website=Globo|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref> The group recorded a self-titled album of pop covers, produced by [[Rick Bonadio]] and released by [[Sony Music Brazil|Sony Music]] on 18 November 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xuxa.com/noticias/pagina/638/cd-do-kidx|title=CD do KidX|website=Xuxa.com|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref> The project was discontinued in 2014 due to low investment and reception.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dgabc.com.br/Noticia/498714/banda-kidx-aposta-em-covers|title=Banda KidX aposta em covers|website=Diário do Grande ABC|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2016, he starred in the play ''Meninos e Meninas'', in which he performed a homosexual kiss.<ref name="purepeople"/> That same year, he auditioned for [[The Voice Brasil season 5|season five]] of ''[[The Voice Brasil]]'', advancing with three approvals after performing "[[Que Sorte a Nossa]]" by [[Matheus & Kauan]], and chose to join [[Michel Teló]]'s team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gshow.globo.com/Bastidores/noticia/bruno-gadiol-explica-escolha-pelo-hit-que-sorte-a-nossa-ja-fez-muito-sentido-na-minha-vida.ghtml|title=Bruno Gadiol explica escolha pelo hit 'Que Sorte a Nossa': 'Já fez muito sentido na minha vida'|website=Globo|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref> He reached the semi-finals, leaving the competition in the final round of Michel Teló's team against Mylena Jardim, who would become the season's winner.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hugogloss.com/index.php/music/voice-mylena-jardim-faz-apresentacao-maravilhosa-de-love-brain-da-riri/|title=The Voice: Mylena Jardim faz apresentação maravilhosa de "Love On The Brain", da Riri|website=Hugo Gloss|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In 2017, he made his television acting debut as the introverted pianist Guto in the [[Malhação: Viva a Diferença|twenty-fifth season]] of ''[[Malhação]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://noticiasdatv.uol.com.br/noticia/novelas/cantor-vira-gala-de-malhacao-e-diz-que-voice-e-mais-facil-do-que-novela--15014|title=Cantor vira galã de Malhação e diz que The Voice é mais fácil que novela|website=UOL|access-date=8 October 2017|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 2015, he enrolled in advertising and publicity at [[Fundação Cásper Líbero]] but dropped out in his first semester to focus on acting, later graduating as a professional actor from Teatro Escola Macunaíma.<ref name="baruerinarede"/> He also studied musical theater at Teen Broadway in 2016.<ref name="baruerinarede"/> On 12 June 2018, he released a music video titled "Seu Costume" in partnership with Gabriel Nandes, using the occasion to publicly come out as gay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.extra.globo.com/tv-e-lazer/bruno-gadiol-ex-malhacao-assume-homossexualidade-em-clipe-seu-costume-22758474.html|title=Bruno Gadiol, ex-'Malhação', assume homossexualidade em clipe 'Seu Costume'|website=Extra|access-date=16 April 2026|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

Cindy Caputo appelée en équipe de France : une première depuis 2012 à l’ASSE !|date=17 October 2024|website=www.leprogres.fr}}</ref> She made her debut on 25 October 2024 in a 3–0 win against [[Jamaica women's national football team|Jamaica]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Les Bleues assurent contre une faible Jamaïque pour la première de Laurent Bonadei|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Les-bleues-assurent-contre-une-faible-jamaique-pour-la-premiere-de-laurent-bonadei/1516294|date=25 October 2024|access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Caputo considers [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Hatem Ben Arfa]] her football inspirations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Caputo, priorité à gauche|url=https://www.fff.fr/article/13633-caputo-priorite-a-gauche.html|date=15 November 2024|access-date=13 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Rosalie Bonenfant''' (born August 26, 1996) is a [[Canada|Canadian]] actress and television host from [[Quebec]].<ref>Patrick Delisle-Crevier, [https://www.7jours.ca/2026/05/21/rosalie-bonenfant-fait-le-point-a-lapproche-de-la-trentaine "Rosalie Bonenfant fait un aveu sur sa relation amoureuse et aborde la trentaine qui approche"]. {{short description|American ice hockey coach}} {{Infobox ice hockey biography | name = Matt McIlvane | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1985|11|2}} | birth_place = [[Naperville, Illinois]], U.S. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | weight_lb = 203 | position = [[Centre (ice hockey)|Center]] | shoots = Right | played_for = [[Eisbären Berlin]]
[[Binghamton Senators]]
[[Peoria Rivermen (AHL)|Peoria Rivermen]] | draft = 251st overall | draft_year = 2004 | draft_team = [[Ottawa Senators]] | career_start = 2008 | career_end = 2011 | career_start_coach = 2011 }} '''Matthew McIlvane''' (born November 2, 1985) is an American professional [[ice hockey]] coach and former player who is currently an assistant coach for the [[Boston Bruins]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). McIlvane was selected in the 8th round of the [[2004 NHL entry draft]] by the [[Ottawa Senators]], and played professionally for four years before retiring due to injury. He has served as the head coach for [[EC Salzburg]] of the [[ICE Hockey League]] (ICEHL) and [[San Diego Gulls]] of the [[American Hockey League]] (AHL). He was an assistant coach for the [[Germany men's national ice hockey team|German national ice hockey team]] at the [[Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2018 Winter Olympics]], where he helped the team to a silver medal. == Playing career == === Amateur === An Illinois native, McIlvane played for the [[Chicago Freeze]] of the [[North American Hockey League]] (NAHL) and the [[Chicago Steel]] of the [[United States Hockey League]] (USHL) for parts of three seasons, scoring twenty goal seasons in his final two seasons before he announced his commitment to play [[college ice hockey]] for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's ice hockey|Ohio State]] starting in the [[2004–05 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2004-05 season]].{{Cite web |title=Six Commit to Ohio State Men’s Hockey Team for 2004-05 – Ohio State Buckeyes |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/news/2003/11/19/six-commit-to-ohio-state-mens-hockey-team-for-2004-05 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Ohio State |language=en}} McIlvane would play four years for Ohio State, helping the team to at at-large bid in his freshman season, and was named an alternate captain for his junior season. Prior to his senior season in [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2007–08]], McIlvane was named captain of the team.{{Cite web |title=McIlvane Named Men’s Hockey Captain – Ohio State Buckeyes |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/news/2007/10/12/mcilvane-named-mens-hockey-captain |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Ohio State |language=en}} === Professional === McIlvane was drafted in the eighth round, 251st overall, by the [[Ottawa Senators]] in the [[2004 NHL entry draft]]. After his collegiate career concluded, McIlvane signed an [[Amateur Try-Out|amateur try-out]] (ATO) contract with the Senators [[American Hockey League]] (AHL) affiliate, the [[Binghamton Senators]].{{Cite web |title=Men’s Hockey: Former Buckeyes Continue to Join Professional Ranks – Ohio State Buckeyes |url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/news/2008/3/25/mens-hockey-former-buckeyes-continue-to-join-professional-ranks |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Ohio State |language=en}} McIlvane would appear in four games for the remainder of the [[2007–08 AHL season|2007–08 season]] for the Senators, scoring a single assist. After the season, McIlvane opted to continue his professional hockey career in Europe, signing with [[Eisbären Berlin]] of the [[Deutsche Eishockey Liga]] (DEL). McIlvane would sit out the beginning of the season while recovering from an elbow injury.{{Cite web |title=Eisbären ohne Braun und McIlvane in Köln {{!}} SPOX |url=https://www.spox.com/eishockey/news/eisbaeren-ohne-raun-und-McmIlvane-in-koeln/134048 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.spox.com |language=de}} Unfortunately for McIlvane, he would only play 14 games with Berlin after returning before his season was cut short after sustaining an injury during a game.{{Cite news |date=2008-11-17 |title=Kreuzbandriss: Saisonende für Matt McIlvane |url=https://www.hockeyweb.de/del/kreuzbandriss-saisonende-f%C3%BCr-matt-mcilvane-26658 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250908145815/https://www.hockeyweb.de/del/kreuzbandriss-saisonende-f%C3%BCr-matt-mcilvane-26658 |archive-date=2025-09-08 |access-date=2026-09-06 |work=Hockeyweb |language=de}} McIlvane would move back to the U.S. after the season, signing with the [[Bloomington PrairieThunder]] of the [[United Hockey League]] (UHL). He scored 11 goals and 13 assists in 62 games with the PrairieThunder before signing a [[professional tryout]] (PTO) contract with the [[Peoria Rivermen (AHL)|Peoria Rivermen]], returning to the AHL.{{Cite web |date=2010-03-12 |title=Rivermen Sign Matt McIlvane To PTO |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/rivermen-sign-matt-mcilvane-to-pto/n-3974221 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=OurSports Central |language=en}} He scored a goal and three assists with the Rivermen in eight games to conclude the season. McIlvane signed with the Rivermen to start the [[2010–11 AHL season|2010–11 season]], but would start his season playing with the PraireThunder, who had joined the [[Central Hockey League]] (CHL). After scoring five points in his first seven games with the PraireThunder, McIlvane was recalled to the Rivermen.{{Cite web |date=2010-11-12 |title=Rivermen Sign Derek Nesbitt to PTO, Recall McIlvane |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/rivermen-sign-derek-nesbitt-to-pto-recall-mcilvane/n-4114867 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=OurSports Central |language=en}} He would play three games with the Rivermen, notching a goal and an assists, before being sent back down to the PraireThunder, although he would not appear with them due to injury.{{Cite web |title=Cyclones Add Former Ohio State Captain Matt McIlvane |url=https://cycloneshockey.com/news/2011/08/cyclones-add-former-ohio-state-captain-matt-mcilvane |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=cycloneshockey.com |language=en}} McIlvane would sign with the [[ECHL]]'s [[Cincinnati Cyclones]] for the 2011-12 season. However, McIlvane would only appear in two games with the Cyclones before suffering from another injury. After the injury, McIlvane retired from professional hockey.{{Cite web |title=Matt McIlvane Announces Retirement from Hockey |url=https://cycloneshockey.com/news/2011/10/matt-mcilvane-announces-retirement-from-hockey |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=cycloneshockey.com |language=en}} == Coaching career == === Early career === McIlvane's head coaching career started soon after he retired, at the age of 26, when he was hired by the [[Danville Dashers (FPHL)|Danville Dashers]] of the [[Federal Prospects Hockey League]] (FPHL) in December 2011. He was the team's third head coach of the season, after the first coach was fired due to a poor start, and the second had to step away due to injury.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-27 |title=Meet hockey’s Ted Lasso: new San Diego Gulls coach Matt McIlvane |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/05/27/meet-hockeys-ted-lasso-new-san-diego-gulls-coach-matt-mcilvane/ |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Orange County Register |language=en-US}} At the time of McIlvane taken over, the Dashers had played 26 games and won none. However, on January 1, 2012, the Dashers faced the defending champions and won 15-1, signaling a turnaround.{{Cite web |date=2021-01-12 |title=EC Red Bull Salzburg's Matt McIlvane: "The dictator era is over" |url=https://www.redbull.com/us-en/theredbulletin/matt-mcilvane-interview-red-bull-salzburg |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Red Bull |language=en-us}} After the season with the Dashers, McIlvane was named an assistant coach of the [[Orlando Solar Bears]].{{Cite web |title=Solar Bears name Matt McIlvane as assistant coach |url=https://orlandosolarbearshockey.com/news/2012/07/solar-bears-name-matt-mcilvane-as-assistant-coach-2286 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=Orlando Solar Bears |language=en}} === Europe === After one season with the Solar Bears, McIlvane decided to make the jump to Europe again, this time for his coaching career. He spent the 2013-14 season as an assistant coach with [[EC Salzburg]] of the [[ICE Hockey League]] (ICEHL). With Salzburg, McIlvane won the league title. After a year with Salzberg, McIlvane was hired as an assistant coach with [[EHC Munchen]] with the [[Deutsche Eishockey Liga]] (DEL). In five years with Munchen, McIlvane won the league title three times. Because of his success of an assistant coach at Munchen, he was selected by head coach [[Marco Sturm]] to be an assistant for him for the [[Germany men's national ice hockey team|German national team]] at the [[Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2018 Winter Olympics]].{{Cite web |date=2026-06-14 |title=The Sunday Read: How Matt McIlvane Landed in Boston as New Assistant Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/the-sunday-read-how-matt-mcilvane-landed-in-boston-as-new-assistant-coach |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}} McIlvane won a silver medal with the team at the Olympics. After five years with Munchen, McIlvane returned to Salzburg, this time as their head coach. At the time of the hiring, McIlvane was the youngest head coach in team history, at 33. McIlvane spent four years at the helm at Salzburg, leading them to the league title in his final two years. In 2021, McIlvane was named an assistant coach for Germany at the [[2021 IIHF World Championship|2021 World Championship]], where they finished in fourth. === San Diego Gulls === On April 23, 2023, McIlvane was announced as the head coach of the [[San Diego Gulls]] of the [[American Hockey League]] (AHL), returning to the U.S. after ten seasons coaching abroad.{{Cite web |title=Anaheim Ducks Name Matt McIlvane Head Coach Of San Diego Gulls {{!}} San Diego Gulls |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/anaheim-ducks-name-matt-mcilvane-head-coach-of-san-diego-gulls |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.sandiegogulls.com |language=en}} McIlvane's Gulls would not make the [[Calder Cup]] playoffs his first two seasons, although there was steady improvement for the team from before his arrival. In McIlvane's third season coaching the team, they managed to make the playoffs, finishing 7th in the Pacific Division. Their 33 wins were the Gulls most wins in a season since the [[2018–19 AHL season|2018–19 season]]. However, they would lose in the opening round in two games to the [[Colorado Eagles]]. On April 15, 2026, the Gulls announced that they had agreed to a multi-year extension with McIlvane to stay as the head coach.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Anaheim Ducks Extend Contract of Gulls Head Coach Matt McIlvane {{!}} San Diego Gulls |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/anaheim-ducks-extend-gulls-coach-matt-mcilvane-apr-15-2026 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.sandiegogulls.com |language=en}} === Boston Bruins === On June 11, 2026, McIlvane was announced as an assistant coach of the [[Boston Bruins]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).{{Cite web |date=2026-06-11 |title=Matt McIlvane Added to Boston Bruins Coaching Staff {{!}} Boston Bruins |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/matt-mcilvane-added-to-boston-bruins-coaching-staff |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}} The move reunited him with head coach [[Marco
